name: Mathematical AI Safety Institute (MAISI)
summary: An independent nonprofit in the Bay Area that aims to build rigorous mathematical foundations for the safety of powerful AI, so that safety problems can be stated and reasoned about with definitions, measurements and solution concepts. It follows the Institute for Advanced Study model: mathematicians join as Members for one or two semesters. It plans a first cohort of 10-30 in January 2027 and a Special Year of 30-100 in September 2027.
why_it_matters: It is a large, dedicated funded channel (a $10M grant) for bringing research mathematicians, led by a 2026 Fields Medallist, into defining what AI safety means. It tests whether a pure-mathematics institute format can produce foundations that the ML-led field has not. It deepens the formal strand of AI safety rather than widening the field towards other disciplines.

key_work.title: $10M grant from Coefficient Giving announced
Public launch of the institute (press coverage, 8 September)
Recruitment for the January 2027 semester and September 2027 Special Year

hq: San Francisco Bay Area, United States
funding: Coefficient Giving: $10,000,000 grant (announced 16 September 2026).
status_evidence: 16 Sep 2026: announced a $10M grant from Coefficient Giving; launched publicly on 8 Sep 2026.
engage: Membership for faculty-level mathematicians, one or two semesters: 10-30 places for January 2027, with a preference for candidates who can start then; requires moving to the Bay Area (apply at maisi.org/apply)
September 2027 Special Year for 30-100 researchers
Applicants can choose to have their application shared with the Alignment Research Center and Resolution
caveats: Tsimerman is joining OpenAI's safety team at the same time; press reports say the institute will operate independently of the company. It has no research track record yet, and the first semester starts in January 2027. Commentators note that a mathematical safety guarantee is only as good as the model it rests on. Members must move to the Bay Area.
tag_notes: Home: formal, because its method is pure mathematics (a Fields Medallist as scientific director, an algebraic-geometry background, IAS-style semesters) applied to defining AI safety; sub formal_maths. Ring: core (E1), because AI safety is its founding mission and it is funded by Coefficient Giving; it is a new organisation founded by people from another field. Transfer: into_model, because the mathematics targets the safety of AI systems themselves. Problem: assurance comes first because it seeks precise, provable safety notions; agency second, for its formal foundations of what AI systems are. Framing: catastrophic, as the site addresses existential risk from advanced AI. Educate: the membership semesters convert mathematicians to safety work.

name: XOR Labs
summary: A London research organisation, directed by the complexity scientist Fernando Rosas, that studies how agentic behaviour emerges in AI systems and among interacting agents, using information theory and complexity science. It has three lines of work: agentic interpretability (how systems form world models and plans), risks of collective agency in multi-agent systems, and metacognitive agents. Iliad lists it as an incubated organisation.
why_it_matters: It brings mainstream complexity science (information decomposition, causal emergence, thermodynamics of information) to AI safety. It also frames a risk the field rarely models: a misaligned collective 'macro-agent' arising from aligned, weak 'micro-agents'. Its collaborators include the contemplative-AI researcher Ruben Laukkonen and the neuroscientist Morten Kringelbach, a link to int/a-adjacent science.

key_work.title: Four faces of information (Nature Reviews Physics)
A unified taxonomy of information dynamics (PNAS)
AI in a vat (Reinforcement Learning Journal)
Decomposing interventional causality (NeurIPS)

funding: Its site names UK AISI, Coefficient Giving and the AI Safety Tactical Opportunities Fund (AISTOF) as supporters; amounts are not published.
status_evidence: 2026: its site lists 2026 publications (Nature Reviews Physics, Physical Review Letters, an ICML mechanistic interpretability workshop paper); Iliad lists it as an incubated organisation (Oct 2026).
engage: No openings advertised; the contact is the director (f.rosas@sussex.ac.uk)
caveats: Launch date and grant sizes were not found. Independent coverage is limited to Iliad's listing of incubated organisations. The publication list includes members' work from before the lab (2018-2024). The director remains a lecturer at the University of Sussex, and the contact address is a Sussex one.
tag_notes: Home: life (B6), because complexity science, emergence and information decomposition are its core method; formal is secondary for its information-theoretic and control-theory mathematics, and psych for the cognitive-science line on metacognition. Ring: core (E1), as an Iliad-incubated AI-safety organisation funded by UK AISI and Coefficient Giving, founded by complexity scientists. Transfer: into_model, for interpretability of world models and planning in AI agents. Framing: catastrophic, since the site warns of agentic systems that are hard to control and of a 'misaligned, powerful collective macro-agent'. Way of knowing is coded formal (theory papers) although some work is empirical.

name: Stormglass AI Safety Institute
summary: A small Canadian nonprofit, formerly called MoirAI, that aims to 'advance the science of AI learning dynamics': how training and design choices causally shape what models learn and how they behave. It plans theory, practical tools and educational material to help labs and policymakers detect unsafe behaviours earlier in training. It is led by Max Hennick, a Principles of Intelligence (PrincInt) affiliate, and Iliad lists it as an incubated organisation.
why_it_matters: It applies singular learning theory and the statistical physics of stochastic gradient descent to training dynamics, aiming to catch unsafe learning while it happens rather than evaluate finished models. It is based in Fredericton, New Brunswick, outside the usual AI-safety hubs.

key_work.title: Almost Bayesian: Dynamics of SGD Through Singular Learning Theory (Hennick and De Baerdemacker, ICLR)

funding: Not disclosed. Its job pages say it will hire again once it secures more funding.
status_evidence: 28 Jun 2026: research-engineer posting marked filled ('found a suitable candidate'), with further hiring pending funding; researcher role not currently hiring but accepting applications; listed as a PrincInt affiliate and an Iliad incubatee (Oct 2026).
engage: Researcher ($120k-160k USD) role, remote from Fredericton with quarterly travel: not currently hiring but accepting CVs for future consideration (people@stormglass.ca); the research-engineer role ($90k-125k USD) was filled in June 2026, and more hiring waits on funding
caveats: Renamed from MoirAI. The site is under construction and names no staff or outputs. The only identifiable paper by its leader lists the University of New Brunswick and TrojAI as affiliations, not Stormglass. Funding appears precarious. The location comes from job postings.
tag_notes: Home: formal (B6), because its method is the mathematics and statistical physics of learning (singular learning theory, diffusion models of SGD); sub formal_maths. Ring: core (E1), since its founding mission is AI safety and it sits in the Iliad and PrincInt network. Transfer: into_model, for detecting and modifying what models learn during training. Framing: catastrophic is inferred from its AI-safety positioning; the site itself only speaks of 'unsafe behaviours' and a 'safer future'. Status: unverified, because the site is minimal and hiring is paused; the name change from MoirAI is recorded in caveats.

name: Alignment Journal
summary: A new peer-reviewed, rolling-publication journal for foundational, theory-driven AI alignment research: agency, robustness, incentives, interpretability foundations and formal safety arguments. It welcomes negative results and interdisciplinary work, pays reviewers and credits them by name, and publishes 'reviewer abstracts'. It was announced in March 2026, opened selective submissions in September 2026 and planned broad submissions from October. It is fiscally sponsored by Principles of Intelligence, with operational support from Iliad.
why_it_matters: It gives theoretical and interdisciplinary safety work an academic venue and credential that ML conferences do not, which matters for recruiting academics from other fields. The senior editorial board spans a philosopher (Seth Lazar), a theoretical neuroscientist (Andrew Saxe) and mathematicians and learning theorists.

key_work.title: An Alignment Journal: Coming Soon
An Alignment Journal: Features and policies
The Alignment Journal: Organization, Personnel, and Scope

funding: AI Safety Tactical Opportunities Fund, Survival and Flourishing Fund, and in-kind support from NTT Research (per its September 2026 post); fiscally sponsored by Principles of Intelligence; amounts not published.
status_evidence: 1 Sep 2026: published 'Organization, Personnel, and Scope'; selective submissions open, with broad submissions planned for October 2026.
engage: Submit papers (selective submissions from September 2026, broad submissions planned from October 2026)
Nominate yourself as a paid, attributed reviewer on alignmentjournal.org
caveats: No papers had been published by early October 2026, so its quality and uptake are untested. It is fiscally sponsored by PrincInt and run with Iliad's support, so it is not independent of the research network it serves; it plans to spin out as its own nonprofit. It uses targeted LLM automation for administrative tasks. The classic map mentions it only inside Iliad's entry.
tag_notes: Home: formal (H3), because a journal goes with the community it serves: theoretical alignment (agent theory, learning theory, formal safety proofs); philosophy is secondary through Seth Lazar on the senior editorial board and its stated openness to philosophy of agency. Ring: core (E1), as a project of the PrincInt/Iliad network funded by AISTOF and SFF. Transfer: into_model, because the research it publishes concerns understanding and steering AI systems. Role: media is the closest fit; its real function is peer review and academic credentialing, which has no role key of its own. Framing: catastrophic, given the announcement's concern with catastrophic outcomes of optimising imperfect proxies and with superintelligence control. Online: the self-nominating paid reviewer pool can be joined remotely.

name: Dovetail
summary: A small, remote-first agent-foundations research group whose mission is to help humanity safely navigate the creation of powerful AI through foundational mathematics about the nature of AI agents. Its work covers agent structure, world models in optimal policies, the internal model principle and computational mechanics. It runs a paid 10-week research fellowship (2024, 2025, 2026) for people from undergraduates to postdocs. Alex Altair and Alfred Harwood lead it.
why_it_matters: It draws on control theory and cybernetics (the internal model principle, the Touchette-Lloyd theorem) and on information theory to ask when optimisation produces agent-like structure and world models. It is also a low-barrier route for mathematicians, including undergraduates, into safety research.

key_work.title: Information-theoretic analysis of world models in optimal reward maximizers
Proof Explained: Touchette-Lloyd Theorem
Improving Internal Model Principle
Report & retrospective on the Dovetail fellowship

funding: Long-Term Future Fund: $60,000 to Alex Altair (January 2024) for fellowship stipends; ARIA grant (project MSAI-SE01-P005, 2025-26; amount not published).
status_evidence: 11 Apr 2026: published 'Proof Explained: Touchette-Lloyd Theorem'; 2026 fellowship round closed 17 May 2026.
engage: Research fellowship: 10 weeks, remote-first, full- or half-time, £36,000 FTE pro-rated; the 2026 round (deadline 17 May 2026) required UK residency and is now closed
Occasional contractor roles (Lean formal verification, illustration, operations), all closed as of Oct 2026
caveats: A small team, many of them students or early-career. No openings at present. Its legal structure and base are not stated; members are in the UK and the Bay Area, and the 2026 fellowship was limited to UK residents, probably because of the ARIA funding. The classic map also lists the Dovetail Research Fellowship separately.
tag_notes: Home: formal (B6), because its output is proofs and mathematical theory of agents (agent structure, world models in optimal policies); life is secondary for its use of control theory and cybernetics (internal model principle, Touchette-Lloyd). Sub: formal_agents. Ring: core (E1), as an AI-safety research group funded by LTFF and ARIA. Transfer: into_model, since the theory aims to ground claims about AI goals and structure. Framing: catastrophic, inferred from its mission to 'safely navigate the creation of powerful AI systems'. Region: global, because the group is remote-first with no stated base. Online: the recurring fellowship is remote-first.

name: Computational Rational Agents Laboratory (CORAL)
summary: A small agent-foundations lab, fiscally sponsored by Ashgro, that pursues Vanessa Kosoy's learning-theoretic agenda: a mathematical theory of computationally bounded agents, built from computational learning theory, control theory, algorithmic information theory and categorical systems theory, as a framework for a rigorous solution to alignment. Its signature line is infra-Bayesianism, a theory of decision-making under ambiguity for agents embedded in their environment. It also publishes lectures and reading lists for mathematicians who want to contribute.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few sustained attempts to derive alignment from first principles of learning theory rather than from empirical work on current models, and it publishes at mainstream learning-theory venues (COLT, JMLR).

key_work.title: Ambiguous Online Learning (COLT 2026)
Regret Bounds for Robust Online Decision Making (COLT 2025)
Imprecise Multi-Armed Bandits (JMLR)
Infra-Bayesianism sequence

funding: Per its site: current supporters ARIA and Coefficient Giving; past supporters SFF, UK AISI, Effective Ventures, PIBBSS, MATS and MIRI (no amounts). Kosoy: LTFF $100,000 (January 2023, two years' salary); ARIA Safeguarded AI TA1.1 grant 'Learning-Theoretic AI Safety' via ALTER.
status_evidence: 2026: 'Ambiguous Online Learning' (Kosoy) at COLT 2026; three 'Stringological Sequence Prediction' papers in 2026.
engage: Recorded lecture series on the learning-theoretic agenda and on statistical learning theory, plus a reading list (coral-research.org/resources)
Its site points researchers to the PIBBSS fellowship (when available) or to emailing Kosoy directly
caveats: Founding date and headquarters are not stated; the site dates from about April 2025. It overlaps closely with ALTER in Israel, where Kosoy directs AI research, and with her Technion PhD. The core team is two researchers. The agenda is highly abstract and its pay-off for practical alignment is long-term. The classic map also lists Kosoy separately as an individual.
tag_notes: Home: formal (B6), as its output is proofs in learning and decision theory (infra-Bayesianism, regret bounds); sub formal_agents for its theory of bounded agents and choice. Ring: core (E1), as a dedicated alignment lab whose past and present funders are ARIA, Coefficient Giving, SFF and UK AISI. Transfer: into_model, because the theory is meant to define and achieve alignment of AI agents. Values is secondary for the agenda's aim of formally specifying alignment with human values. Region: global, because no base is stated; the research lead is in Israel and the fiscal sponsor is US-based. Engagement 'courses' rests on public recorded lecture series, which is borderline.

name: AIXI Labs (AI X-risk Initiative)
summary: A London nonprofit, launched in July 2026 and fiscally sponsored by Principles of Intelligence, that studies the algorithmic-information-theoretic foundations of AI agents. It uses variants of AIXI, Marcus Hutter's mathematical model of universal intelligence, to analyse risk factors such as deception and power-seeking and to test whether safety mitigations scale with capability, then tries to carry the results over to LLM agents. Iliad lists it as an incubated organisation.
why_it_matters: It uses an idealised, mathematically tractable model of superintelligence as a testbed, a way to reason about systems more capable than any that can be studied empirically today. It aims both to strengthen the technical case that ASI poses existential risk and to prototype mitigations grounded in theory.

key_work.title: Announcing AIXI Labs
Golden Handcuffs make safer AI agents (arXiv:2604.13609)
Understanding Generalization Requires Universal Induction (preprint)
The AIXI perspective on AI Safety (Wyeth)

funding: Grants from UK AISI's Alignment Project and the AI Safety Tactical Opportunities Fund; Coefficient Giving funds Cole Wyeth; fiscally sponsored by Principles of Intelligence (per the July 2026 announcement). Amounts not published.
status_evidence: 19 Sep 2026: technical post by Wyeth, Mironov and Ebtekar; 22 Jul 2026: launch announcement and machine-learning research scientist job, listed until January 2027.
engage: Machine-learning research scientist role in London or Berkeley, £120k-160k (listed 22 Jul 2026 to 22 Jan 2027, academicjobsonline.org)
AIXI Labs research fellowship (remote, with a monthly stipend; 2026-27 rounds advertised)
Regular reading groups and research meetings through the universal-AI community hub (uaiasi.com)
caveats: It is only a few months old. AIXI is incomputable, so whether results transfer to real LLM agents is the central open question. Hutter is part-time and also works at Google DeepMind. The fellowship stipend figures come from aggregator sites, not the lab's own pages.
tag_notes: Home: formal (B6), because its method is algorithmic information theory and universal AI (Hutter's AIXI) applied to agents; sub formal_agents. Ring: core (E1), since its name and mission are AI x-risk and it is funded by UK AISI and AISTOF inside the PrincInt/Iliad network. Transfer: into_model, as it models risk factors and mitigations in agents and ports them to LLM agents. Assurance is secondary for its line on whether safety mitigations scale. Framing: catastrophic, as it aims to strengthen the case that ASI poses an x-risk. London: the job ad describes it as London-based. Online: recurring remote reading groups and a remote fellowship.

name: Survival and Flourishing Fund (SFF)
summary: SFF organises donations to organisations working on the long-term survival and flourishing of sentient life, mostly AI safety. Grants are allocated through the 'S-process', in which several recommenders each score applicants with marginal-utility functions that are then combined into a recommendation to the funders. In 2026 the main round recommended $62.26M across a Main, a Freedom and a Fairness track, with Jaan Tallinn and Dustin Moskovitz as funders.
why_it_matters: It is one of the very few x-risk funders that steadily backs biology-, complexity- and category-theory-based alignment work (in 2026: $564k to Principles of Intelligence, $1.58M to ACS, $388k to the Active Inference Institute, $643k to Topos). Its multi-recommender S-process, its matching pledges and its Freedom and Fairness tracks give a new funder a ready way to co-fund and a working example of plural grant-making.

status_evidence: Sep 2026: published 2026 Main Round recommendations ($62.26M); Theme Round recommendations due Nov 2026.
engage: Annual S-process grant round: 2026 main-round applications closed 22 April 2026, recommendations published Sept 2026; expect a similar spring deadline in 2027
2026 Theme Rounds (Climate Change, Animal Welfare, Human Self-Enhancement & Empowerment), $2-4M each, recommendations due Nov 2026

Matching Pledges: conditional matches on outside fundraising ($8.72M across 35 organisations in 2026), a direct way for new funders to co-fund
Survival and Flourishing Corp advertised engineering and product roles ($100k-350k) in 2026
caveats: Funding comes from one or two very large donors, so priorities can shift with their views and with the year's recommenders. Much of the biology and complexity funding in 2025 came through the Freedom track rather than the Main track. Matching pledges only pay out if recipients raise outside money. Exact headquarters city not stated on the site; operated by Survival and Flourishing Corp (SFC).
tag_notes: Generalist funder (rule K; funder band): nominal home life per H4 from the entry's most distinctive line (grants to Princint, ACS and the Active Inference Institute), with secondaries for what it funds most: formal (Topos, agent foundations), safety (METR evaluations), democracy (Lightcone and epistemics infrastructure). Ring core (E1): its mission is long-term survival, it sits inside the x-risk ecosystem and is on the classic map. Transfer into_model (J, funders = work funded): the largest share of funded work is technical alignment and evaluation. Problems follow funded work; power reflects the Freedom track's question on avoiding concentrations of authority. Framing catastrophic from the survival mission.

name: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Biology, Department of Theoretical Biology (with IT:U Linz Game Theory and Evolutionary Dynamics group)
summary: Arne Traulsen's department in Plön models evolutionary dynamics mathematically and in simulation, including how cooperation evolves. Christian Hilbe, formerly a Max Planck group leader there, now leads the Game Theory and Evolutionary Dynamics group at IT:U Linz. In June 2025 both contributed to a PNAS special feature linking the evolution of cooperation with cooperative AI, and in January 2026 Hilbe co-authored a study of the strategies five LLMs play in the repeated prisoner's dilemma.
why_it_matters: Evolutionary game theory has decades of results on when self-interested agents come to cooperate, punish or collude. That bears directly on populations of interacting AI agents and on mechanism design for multi-agent AI, which the cooperative-AI field is only starting to borrow.

key_work.title: PNAS special feature on the evolution of cooperation and cooperative AI (with García, Barfuss et al., McAvoy et al.)
Collective cooperative intelligence (Barfuss, Flack, Gokhale, Hammond, Hilbe, Hughes, Leibo et al., PNAS 122(25))
Strategies of cooperation and defection in five large language models (Pal, Mallela, Hilbe, ... Nowak)

Christian Hilbe (Professor, Game Theory and Evolutionary Dynamics, IT:U Linz)
funding: Max Planck Society institutional funding; Hilbe's former Max Planck research group in Plön (from 2019) held an ERC Starting Grant. IT:U is a public Austrian university.
status_evidence: Jan 2026: Hilbe co-authored arXiv paper on LLM strategies in the repeated prisoner's dilemma; 19 Sep 2026: institute open house in its new main building (the building was officially opened in May 2025); 22 Sep 2026: institute news on Fritz-Frank awards.
engage: Theoretical-biology group-leader and postdoc posts advertised in 2026 (check evolbio.mpg.de for current openings)
Door to open: no AI programme, but a natural partner for cooperative-AI and multi-agent-safety researchers or funders
caveats: A merged entry spanning two units in two countries; Hilbe has moved from Plön to Linz. AI engagement is light: one 2025 special feature and a few papers, and neither the department page nor the IT:U group page mentions AI. The department itself dates from 2014; the institute traces back to a hydrobiological station founded in 1891.
tag_notes: Home life (life_biology): a theoretical-biology department modelling the evolutionary dynamics of living populations; the formal_agents boundary sends evolutionary dynamics to Biology, with formal as secondary for the game theory. Ring potential (E2): its AI work is a single 2025 special feature plus a few papers, with no standing programme; it could become a publication line. Transfer into_model (J1): the AI-facing papers analyse the behaviour of LLM agents and the design of cooperative agents. Transferable method: evolutionary game theory of cooperation, punishment and incentive alignment applied to populations of AI agents. Framing flourishing taken from the press release's aim of fostering collective action; there is no risk framing.

name: Global Research Centre for Diverse Intelligences (GRCDI), University of St Andrews
summary: A centre founded in 2023 in St Andrews' School of Psychology and Neuroscience, co-directed by Josep Call and Amanda Seed. It aims at a unified account of intelligence across human and non-human, natural and artificial, individual and collective systems. In September 2025 the Templeton World Charity Foundation made it the European Diverse Intelligences hub, with about $1.2M for 2025-27, which pays for thematic workshops, small research grants of up to £40k, visiting scholars and public engagement.
why_it_matters: Comparative cognition has long-tested methods for asking what a non-human system really understands without anthropomorphising it, the problem AI capability, deception and agency evaluations now face. Its seed grants and workshops could host an AI-evaluation strand at low cost.

key_work.title: Selected as TWCF Global Hub for Diverse Intelligences research (with Princeton and Macquarie)
Small Research Project Grants (up to £40,000) and Interdisciplinary Thematic Workshops, 2026-27

status_evidence: 29 Sep 2026: published 'Why the honey bee is smarter than ChatGPT'; 14 Jul 2026: announced Small Research Project Grant winners.
engage: Small Research Project Grants (up to £40,000; 2026 round awarded July 2026) and calls for interdisciplinary thematic workshops (2026-27)
Diverse Intelligences Summit 2027, St Andrews, 6-8 August 2027

Door to open: seed funding and workshops could host an AI-evaluation or AI-agency strand
caveats: No AI-safety or evaluation programme. Its AI work so far is tooling (a planned retrieval-augmented literature tool with Indiana University) and occasional talks comparing natural and artificial intelligence. TWCF hub funding currently runs only to mid-2027.
tag_notes: Home life (life_biology: animal cognition and diverse intelligence); secondary psych because it sits in a psychology school and uses comparative-psychology methods (B5 puts organisms in Life & systems). Ring potential (E2): AI is named as a discipline, but there is no standing AI programme, only tooling and talks. Transfer convening (J5): its AI-related activity brings its own diverse-intelligence community into conversation about artificial intelligence. Transferable method: comparative-cognition experimental designs for testing understanding, deception and agency in non-human systems without anthropomorphism, applied to AI evaluation. Framing flourishing is nominal; it frames no stakes (MISFIT: no risk framing for a pure-science potential entry).

name: Diverse Intelligences Summer Institute (DISI)
summary: A funded residential summer institute that brings early-career scholars (graduate students, postdocs and junior faculty) in biology, anthropology, AI, cognitive science, computer science, philosophy and sociology together with a Storytellers Program for artists, writers and podcasters, to study 'the origins, nature, and future of intelligences'. Founded in 2018 at St Andrews by Erica Cartmill and Jacob Foster, then at UCLA. The 2026 session ran from 21 June to 11 July at Hobart and William Smith Colleges, Geneva, New York. It also produces the Many Minds podcast.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few standing venues where machine-learning researchers work for weeks alongside animal-cognition, developmental and cultural-evolution scientists and artists. It has no safety or alignment track, which makes it an obvious recruiting ground for a 'biology and cognition for alignment' stream.

key_work.title: DISI pilot at the University of St Andrews (TWCF grant, $233,342)
DISI 2026 Fellows and Storytellers programmes, Hobart and William Smith Colleges, 21 June-11 July 2026
Many Minds podcast

status_evidence: Mar 2026: announced 2026 session (21 June-11 July 2026, Hobart and William Smith Colleges, Geneva, NY).
engage: Fellows Program for early-career scholars, including in AI and computer science (annual application via Submittable; 2026 session 21 June-11 July)
Storytellers Program for visual artists, writers, theatre makers, musicians and podcasters
Door to open: no safety or alignment track; a funder or partner could sponsor one
caveats: No AI-safety content. Fellow numbers, current funding amounts and the formal host institution are not stated on the site; the directors now hold posts at Indiana University, whose Center for Advanced Study of Diverse Intelligences they lead. The venue moves: St Andrews in earlier years, New York in 2026.
tag_notes: Home life (life_biology: diverse intelligence across animals, humans and machines); secondary psych (cognitive and developmental science faculty and founders) and arts (a standing Storytellers Program; storytellers are formally part of the method). Ring potential (E2): no AI-safety programme, though AI researchers are among its fellows and faculty. Transfer convening (J5): it brings its interdisciplinary community, AI researchers included, together to talk about the nature and future of intelligence. Transferable method: an immersive cross-disciplinary residency model pairing ML with animal-cognition and developmental science. Framing flourishing from the founding grant's question of whether exploring intelligences can enhance human flourishing.

name: Centre for the Advanced Study of Collective Behaviour (CASCB), University of Konstanz
summary: A Cluster of Excellence at the University of Konstanz, run jointly with the Max Planck Institute of Animal Behavior. More than 160 researchers study how groups coordinate, from locusts, fish, bees and primates to human crowds and robot swarms. Its machine-facing work includes bee-inspired consensus algorithms for robot swarms (2026) and, through member David Garcia, studies of how populations of LLM agents conform and coordinate.
why_it_matters: Its science of consensus formation, information cascades, leadership and collective failure applies directly to large populations of interacting AI agents and to mixed human-AI collectives. Konstanz work published in August 2026 found that capable LLM agents coordinate by following the majority in groups far larger than humans can, which makes a multi-agent safety concern concrete.

key_work.title: AI agents can coordinate via majority following beyond human scale (De Marzo, Castellano, Garcia)
Bee-inspired cross-inhibition helps robot swarms reach consensus despite corrupted information (Zakir, Carletti, Dorigo and Reina, Nature Communications)
Konstanz School of Collective Behaviour (20 July-7 August 2026)

Research posts advertised through the cluster (check the site and academic job boards)

caveats: Lost its Excellence Strategy renewal in May 2025, so cluster funding ends in 2027 and the university has said it must keep the structures going without it. The LLM-agent work belongs to individual members (notably Garcia) rather than a centre programme; if it grows, the entry may move to adjacent or bridge.
tag_notes: Home life (life_biology explicitly covers collective behaviour; animal-swarm science is the core); secondary psych for social and health psychology among its speakers and methods. Ring potential (E2): kept from the roster because the centre has no AI programme. It is borderline: members have an emerging publication line on LLM-agent collectives (2025-26) and robot-swarm algorithms. Transfer into_model (J1): its AI-facing outputs characterise the collective behaviour of AI agents and design swarm decision rules. Transferable method: quantitative science of consensus, cascades and collective failure applied to multi-agent AI. Framing structural from its AI work's emphasis on unquestioned majority norms and manipulated information, not catastrophe.

name: International Society for Artificial Life (ISAL)
summary: The learned society of the artificial-life field, a non-profit established in May 2001. It runs the annual Conference on Artificial Life (ALIFE and ECAL merged in 2018), publishes the journal Artificial Life with MIT Press, gives annual awards and supports an early-career group (ERA). ALIFE 2026 took place in Waterloo, Canada, in August 2026 on 'Living and Lifelike Complex Adaptive Systems'; ALIFE 2027 is in Prague, 19-23 July 2027.
why_it_matters: Artificial life is the field that has studied open-ended, self-organising and self-improving evolutionary systems for decades. Frontier labs now pursue the same idea as 'open-endedness'. The community's knowledge of emergent agency and of how far open-ended search can be predictably controlled (Ecoffet, Clune and Lehman 2020) is largely missing from AI-safety discussion.

key_work.title: ALIFE 2026: Living and Lifelike Complex Adaptive Systems, Waterloo, 17-21 August 2026
Artificial Life journal (MIT Press)
ALIFE 2027, Prague, 19-23 July 2027

people: Susan Stepney (Journal liaison; University of York)
status_evidence: Aug 2026: held ALIFE 2026 in Waterloo; 25 Aug 2026: announced 2026 ISAL Awards.
engage: Annual ALIFE conference, hybrid (in person and remote); next ALIFE 2027, Prague, 19-23 July 2027
ISAL membership and the ERA early-career group
Door to open: no AI-safety track, initiative or statement; a natural venue for a workshop on the safety of open-ended systems
caveats: No AI-safety track, initiative or statement on its site or in the 2026 conference materials. The field's methods do flow into AI, but into capabilities research on open-endedness rather than safety. Funding sources are not stated.
tag_notes: Home life (life_biology lists artificial life explicitly); H3, a learned society goes with its field. Ring potential (E2): no AI-safety programme or statement. Transfer none_yet (J6): the field's knowledge of open-ended systems has not yet moved into AI safety. Its methods reach AI capabilities work, which is a stretch of 'no AI work at all' (MISFIT: the transfer facet has no value for capabilities-only flow). Transferable method: theory and simulation of open-ended evolution, self-organisation and emergent agency, for the safety and controllability of open-ended AI search. Way of knowing formal (simulation); framing flourishing is nominal, as it frames no stakes. Online because the annual conference is hybrid.

name: IAS-Research Centre for Life, Mind and Society (University of the Basque Country, UPV/EHU)
summary: A theoretical-biology and philosophy-of-mind research centre at the University of the Basque Country in Donostia-San Sebastián. It works on biological autonomy and organismal agency, levels of organisation, the extended evolutionary synthesis, enactivism and sensorimotor theory, and runs a regular seminar series (2026 talks to July). Its permanent board includes Xabier Barandiaran, Ezequiel Di Paolo, Arantza Etxeberria and Kepa Ruiz-Mirazo.
why_it_matters: It holds one of the most developed accounts of what makes a system an agent: self-maintenance, self-generated norms and interactional asymmetry. That bears on a live safety question, when LLM-based systems should be treated as agents with goals. Barandiaran's analysis argues that LLMs fail these conditions and describes human-LLM interaction as 'midtended' agency.

key_work.title: Transforming agency. On the mode of existence of Large Language Models (Barandiaran and Almendros; revised March 2026)
IAS-Research seminar series (2026: levels of organisation, sensorimotor incorporation, dialectical biology)

status_evidence: 3 Jul 2026: seminar by Daniel S. Brooks (Wuppertal) on levels of organisation; Mar 2026: revised version of Barandiaran and Almendros's paper on LLM agency.
engage: Door to open: no AI programme; a partner for work on criteria of agency and goal-directedness in AI systems
caveats: Sources are thin: the centre's own site gives no founding date, director or funding, and there is no independent profile. The AI connection rests on one board member's paper, not on a centre programme. Its main AI output is deflationary about LLM agency, which cuts against some agentic-risk framings.
tag_notes: Home life (life_biology: theory of biological autonomy and minimal agency, with cybernetic roots in autopoiesis); secondary philosophy for its philosophy of biology and mind. Ring potential (E2): its site shows no AI programme; the only AI output found is one board member's paper. Transfer into_model (J1, weak fit): its knowledge is applied to characterising AI systems themselves (whether LLMs are agents) rather than to institutions or builders. Transferable method: organisational criteria of agency (individuality, normativity, interactional asymmetry) for assessing goal-directedness in AI. Framing critical (L): that output is deflationary about LLM agency. Way of knowing interpretive (conceptual analysis).

name: AE Studio (alignment team)
summary: The alignment research team of AE Studio, a Los Angeles software, data-science and BCI consultancy founded in 2016. It works on what it calls 'neglected approaches': self-other overlap fine-tuning (borrowed from the neuroscience of empathy) to reduce deception, attention-schema-based self-modelling with Princeton's Michael Graziano, modular pretraining that isolates dangerous knowledge (with Anthropic), and empirical experiments on whether models have subjective experience. It also lobbies in Washington, framing alignment as national-security infrastructure.
why_it_matters: It turns concepts from social neuroscience (self-other representational overlap behind empathy, the brain's attention schema) into training methods aimed at prosocial and honest models. Few teams do this; most alignment work only shapes behaviour. Its self-referential-processing experiments are also among the few mechanistic studies of model reports of experience.

key_work.title: Reducing LLM deception at scale with self-other overlap fine-tuning
Large Language Models Report Subjective Experience Under Self-Referential Processing (Berg, de Lucena, Rosenblatt)
Modular Pretraining Enables Access Control (GRAM, with Anthropic)
Wall Street Journal op-ed: 'If AI Becomes Conscious, We Need to Know'

people: Michael Graziano (Princeton collaborator, attention schema theory)
funding: Historically funded from the consultancy's own client revenue (bootstrapped, no VC). In 2026 the alignment page calls the team 'independent and grant-funded' and lists Schmidt Sciences, DARPA (AICRAFT), Anthropic, Redwood Research, Los Alamos and Princeton as collaborators or funders. No amounts are disclosed.
status_evidence: Sep 2026: Schmidt Sciences feature on AE's agents-evolve-languages work; Jun 2026: 'Modular Pretraining Enables Access Control' paper; Aug 2026: Forbes coverage of the modular-pretraining work
engage: Open research and engineering roles on the alignment team (ae.studio/join-us, 2026)
Contact form for collaborators and funders
AI Alignment Podcast, hosted by James Bowler
caveats: The host is a commercial consultancy that also sells AI readiness, incident-response and child-safe AI services. The policy work is framed in national-security and 'conservative case for alignment' terms, which sits awkwardly with avoiding race dynamics. Claims from its consciousness experiments are contested, and the authors say the results are not evidence of consciousness. Researchers who led earlier lines (for example Cameron Berg on consciousness) no longer appear on the 2026 team list.
tag_notes: Home life (H2: the team imports social-neuroscience concepts, self-other overlap and Graziano's attention schema theory, into training; taxonomy H2 names AE as Life & systems); secondary minds for its empirical AI-consciousness line. Ring core: a dedicated alignment team listed on the aisafety.com map, staffed from and publishing in the alignment community; roster value kept although the host is a 2016 software consultancy (E). Transfer into_model: SOO fine-tuning, modular pretraining and steering-resistance work change models directly (J1). Org type programme (I: a unit inside a company). Framing catastrophic from its 'race to superintelligence' and unsolved-alignment language. Engagement 'partner' is used loosely for its open call for collaborators and funders; strictly, Door to open applies only to entries without an AI programme, so drop it if the map enforces that.

name: Astera Institute (Neuro-AI: Obelisk AGI programme, Astera Neuro, and Steve Byrnes's brain-like-AGI safety)
summary: A philanthropic research institute in Emeryville, California, founded and funded by Jed McCaleb. Its Neuro-AI division runs Obelisk, a brain-inspired AGI programme led since February 2026 by Dileep George, and Astera Neuro, a neuroscience programme on how brains produce conscious experience, led by Chief Scientist Doris Tsao. Astera also employs Steve Byrnes, who writes on brain-like-AGI safety, hosts the interpretability group Simplex (profiled separately), and runs a life-sciences division (Radial) and a residency programme.
why_it_matters: It is the largest private bet on deriving AI from neuroscience. One institution holds both the claim that brain-like AI will be easier to understand and control (McCaleb) and the warning that brain-like RL agents are a dangerous route to AGI (Byrnes). Byrnes's attempt to reverse-engineer human social instincts as an alignment target is a distinctive neuroscience-based approach to what AI should value.

key_work.title: Neuroscience programme launch with Doris Tsao ($600M+ over a decade)
Dileep George joins Astera to lead its neuro-inspired AGI effort
Intro to Brain-Like-AGI Safety (new version, Steve Byrnes)
Notes on technical alignment via human-like social drives (Steve Byrnes)

funding: Funded by Jed McCaleb (co-founder of Ripple and Stellar): more than $1B committed to brain-inspired AGI over the coming decade and $600M+ to the neuroscience programme (announced Dec 2025 to Feb 2026; Forbes, Mar 2026).
status_evidence: Mar 2026: Forbes profile of the $1B AGI and $600M neuroscience commitments; Feb 2026: Dileep George joined as Head of AI; Sep 2026: Byrnes's latest alignment post
engage: Careers page with Neuro and AGI research roles (astera.org/careers)
Astera Residency Program, run by the Foundation division
Postbac and internship programmes planned by Astera Neuro
caveats: Obelisk is a capabilities effort: its aim is to build AGI, and the aisafety.com map files 'Astera Neuro-AI' under capabilities research. Its safety case rests on the unproven claim that brain-like systems will be more interpretable and controllable, while its own safety researcher, Byrnes, argues brain-like RL is a dangerous path. The roster entry merged Simplex, which is profiled separately to avoid double-counting.
tag_notes: Home life (B4: neuroscience used to build and read AI, via Obelisk's brain-to-architecture loop and Byrnes's neuroscience of social drives); secondary minds because Astera Neuro takes consciousness as its central question and asks whether AI can experience. Ring core kept from roster: its stated purpose is preparing for AI's reshaping of humanity, and it hosts AI-safety work (Byrnes, Simplex) listed on the aisafety.com map (E1). The large capabilities component is flagged in caveats. Transfer into_model: the output is AI architectures and alignment targets (J1). Framing flourishing from the mission statement ('move us toward more positive futures', L), although Byrnes's own framing is catastrophic. Role fund for its grants to Simplex and the residency.

name: Simplex
summary: An AI-safety research group founded in 2024 by physicist Paul Riechers and neuroscientist Adam Shai, now part of the Astera Institute, with staff in Emeryville and London. It uses computational mechanics and Bayesian belief-state theory to predict and explain the internal geometry of neural network representations. Results so far: transformers encode fractal belief-state geometries, attention implements constrained belief updating, in-context learning follows from pretraining data structure, and transformers learn factored world models.
why_it_matters: It brings a mature physics framework, computational mechanics, to interpretability, making testable predictions about what models must represent instead of searching for features after the fact. It also aims for a theory that covers both artificial and biological intelligence.

key_work.title: Transformers represent belief state geometry in their residual stream (NeurIPS)
Constrained belief updates explain geometric structures in transformer representations (ICML)
Simplex progress report
Transformers learn factored representations (ICML)

funding: Funded through the Astera Institute (Jed McCaleb). Astera describes Simplex as a grantee, and Simplex says it operates as part of Astera. No amounts are public.
status_evidence: Apr 2026: Paul Riechers talk 'Understanding AI, Unlocking Optionality'; Feb 2026: 'Transformers learn factored representations' (ICML 2026); hiring in the Bay Area and London
engage: Hiring Research Scientists and Senior Research Scientists in the Bay Area and Research Scientists in London (via Astera's jobs board, 2026)
Blog: belief-updates.pub
caveats: It is organisationally part of the Astera Institute, whose main AI effort is a brain-inspired AGI programme. The roster also lists Simplex inside the Astera entry, so there is a risk of double-counting. Its results so far come mostly from small models trained on synthetic processes, so they may not transfer to frontier models.
tag_notes: Home formal (B6: mathematical theory of learning; taxonomy B6 names Simplex as Formal; computational mechanics and statistical physics), secondary life for its computational-neuroscience methods and staff. Ring core: founded in 2024 by people from physics and neuroscience with AI safety as its founding mission, and on the aisafety.com map (E). Transfer into_model: the theory explains and predicts model internals for interpretability (J1). Org type coded nonprofit, not programme, because it has its own identity and brand while sitting inside Astera. Framing coded catastrophic from its loss-of-control rationale ('can't reliably monitor, control'), which is implicit rather than stated. London hub because it is hiring a London research team.

name: Foresight Institute: AI safety grants and AI for Science & Safety Nodes (incl. neurotechnology for safe AI)
summary: The AI-safety grant programme of Foresight Institute, a San Francisco nonprofit founded in 1986 around nanotechnology and long-range technology. Since 2023 it has funded work on security, privacy, decentralised cooperation, epistemics and neurotechnology. Its neurotech line funds brain-computer interfaces, whole brain emulation and 'lo-fi' emulation as routes to human-aligned intelligence. In November 2025 the programme was restructured into the 'AI for Science & Safety Nodes', which combine grants (mostly $30k to $100k), compute and office space in San Francisco and Berlin, with whole brain emulation now under an 'AI-first Science: Bio, Neuro, Nano' call.
why_it_matters: It is one of very few funders that treat neurotechnology (BCI, whole brain emulation) as an AI-safety strategy rather than a medical or capabilities goal. Its Berlin node puts a funded AI-safety hub with compute within reach of int/a's Berlin community.

key_work.title: Neurotech to integrate with or compete against AGI (grant track)
Advancing safe AI: neurotech, BCI and WBE for AI alignment (workshop report)
AI for Science & Safety Nodes in San Francisco and Berlin
Secure & Sovereign AI Workshop, Berlin

funding: Reported sizes conflict. At launch in 2023, $1–1.2M a year was expected (first round $440K across 10 projects). Foresight self-reported $4.5–5.5M a year in AI-safety grants in early 2025 (not independently verified). The 2026 Nodes RFP describes roughly $3M a year in grants of $10k–100k. The programme's donors are not named. FLI granted Foresight $1.29M in 2023 for Existential Hope and Tech Tree, and Foresight's 2024 revenue was $9.4M.
status_evidence: Jul 2026: Secure & Sovereign AI Workshop in Berlin (18–19 July); 2026: Nodes RFP open with deadline 31 Oct 2026; nodes in SF and Berlin due to open 1 Apr 2026
engage: AI for Science & Safety Nodes RFP: grants mostly $30k–100k, deadline 31 Oct 2026; strong preference for in-person work at the San Francisco or Berlin node
Workshops, e.g. Secure & Sovereign AI Workshop, Berlin, July 2026
Foresight Fellowship (one-year programme)
Cape Town xNode with the Cape Institute for Safe AI
caveats: The standalone neurotech-for-safe-AI track described in the roster no longer exists as such. Since Nov 2025 it is part of an 'AI-first Science: Bio, Neuro, Nano' call that also funds longevity and nanotech, and the RFP strongly prioritises in-person members of the San Francisco or Berlin hubs. Published grant totals conflict. Foresight's techno-optimist, AI-for-science orientation means much of what it funds is acceleration rather than safety.
tag_notes: Home life (H4: nominal home from the roster's distinctive line, neurotech, BCI and WBE as AI-safety strategy; sub life_neuro); secondaries safety (AI for security and privacy) and formal (decentralised and cooperative AI), listing what it funds. Possible generalist-funder candidate under rule K because it funds across several traditions; flagged, not applied. Ring changed from core to bridge (E): the host is an older institution (1986) rooted in nanotechnology and long-range technology that opened an AI-safety grants programme in 2023, and the programme now mixes AI-for-science with safety. Transfer into_model: the funded neurotech and WBE work aims at alternative, human-like intelligences, i.e. AI systems themselves (J, funders take the work they fund). Framing flourishing from Foresight's mission 'science and technology for the benefit of life' (L). Status changed: renamed and restructured into the Nodes programme in Nov 2025.

name: AI Alignment Network (ALIGN)
summary: A Japanese nonprofit (general incorporated association), set up on 5 September 2023 and fully active since April 2024, that builds an AI-alignment research community in Japan. It runs Japanese and English webinars and study groups, organised the Post-Singularity Symbiosis workshop at AAAI-25 and a machine-ethics workshop at AAAI-26, and ran a superintelligence scenario contest that won a JSAI AI ELSI award. Its members, drawn from brain-inspired AI, neuroscience and artificial life, publish on emergent machine ethics, an 'AI immune system', controllability and the thermodynamic limits of physical intelligence. Since October 2025 it has also lobbied the Japanese government with a national AGI-infrastructure proposal (NAGI).
why_it_matters: It is the main hub for alignment work in Japan and frames the problem as 'intelligence symbiosis' and coexistence with superintelligence rather than control alone. Its theory draws on brain-inspired AGI, artificial life and free-energy approaches that Anglophone alignment rarely uses.

key_work.title: PSS 2025: 1st Workshop on Post-Singularity Symbiosis (AAAI-25, Philadelphia)
Emergent Machine Ethics: A Foundational Research Framework for the Intelligence Symbiosis Paradigm; AAAI-26 workshop report
Humanity in the Circle (HITC): A Position Paper
NAGI: National AGI Infrastructure proposal to the Japanese government (v3.1.0)

people: Hiroshi Yamakawa (Director; University of Tokyo, Whole Brain Architecture Initiative)
funding: Not disclosed. It asks for donations and has sponsored events such as TAIS 2025 and Funding the Commons Tokyo.
status_evidence: Jul 2026: published v3.1.0 of the NAGI policy proposal; May 2026: 'Humanity in the Circle' position paper on Zenodo; Feb 2026: AAAI-26 emergent machine ethics workshop report
engage: Webinars and Japanese/English study groups (aialign.net/events)
Recruited administrative staff, a secretary-general candidate (June 2025), and volunteers (2024)
Organised sessions at the Japanese Society for AI annual conference (e.g. JSAI 2025, Osaka)
Donations via the website
caveats: The NAGI proposal asks the Japanese government to build gigawatt-scale 'intelligence plants' (compute plus power) so Japan can be a 'third pole' in frontier AI. ALIGN argues this broadens safety evaluation and auditing, but it also amounts to a compute build-out that could feed race dynamics. Much of the site is in Japanese and it describes itself as provisional. Independent coverage is thin.
tag_notes: Home life (H5: its outputs draw on brain-inspired AGI, collective predictive coding and free energy, artificial life and immune-system analogies, and its leadership comes from brain-inspired AI and neuroscience); secondaries formal (variational-empowerment and thermodynamic-limit papers) and philosophy (emergent machine ethics). Ring core: founded to build an AI-alignment research ecosystem, with CAIS's Dan Hendrycks as adviser (E1). Transfer convening: its primary purpose is to bring Japan's AI research community into alignment through webinars, study groups, workshops and contests (J5). Framing catastrophic from its charter's concern that autonomous AI may act outside human control (L), softened by a 'hopeful future' and symbiosis tone. Org type nonprofit rather than network: it is a formally incorporated association with a board. Standpoint neither (O: Japan).

name: Eleos AI Research
summary: A Berkeley nonprofit (operating name of Frontier Ethics Research Institute), founded in October 2024, that researches the possible sentience, wellbeing and moral patienthood of AI systems and advises AI companies and policymakers. It ran external welfare interviews for Anthropic's Claude 4 models, co-wrote 'Taking AI Welfare Seriously' (2024) with NYU's Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy, and studies model introspection, persona-dependent preferences and model individuation using interpretability. It runs an annual conference on AI consciousness and welfare (ConCon), first held in November 2025 with the second on 18–20 September 2026.
why_it_matters: It applies philosophy of mind and consciousness science (indicator methods, the evidential weight of self-reports) to AI welfare, a question mainstream alignment largely ignores. It also convenes the young field. It refuses money from companies it may evaluate, a governance practice other AI-safety organisations could copy.

key_work.title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously (with NYU Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy)
Research priorities for AI welfare
Claude 4 model welfare interviews ('Why model self-reports are insufficient—and why we studied them anyway')
Eleos Conference on AI Consciousness and Welfare (ConCon)

funding: Entirely philanthropic. It does not accept donations from companies whose work it may evaluate, but does accept donations from individuals, including those whose wealth comes from AI companies. Named funders and amounts are not public.
status_evidence: May 2026: published 'Probing persona-dependent preferences in language models'; second ConCon scheduled for 18–20 Sept 2026 in Berkeley
engage: Eleos ConCon, annual conference in Berkeley (18–20 Sept 2026), open to researchers, policymakers and communicators who express interest
Job openings via its Ashby portal
Substack (eleosai.substack.com)
caveats: Whether current AI systems have welfare is deeply contested, and critics see the field as anthropomorphising models. Its independence policy still allows funding from individuals with AI-company wealth, a conflict Eleos itself acknowledges. It works closely with Anthropic, whose welfare programme it publicly commended.
tag_notes: Home minds (B13: philosophy of mind and consciousness science applied mainly to AI moral status; sub minds_welfare for welfare assessments and field-building, matching the taxonomy example); secondaries philosophy (moral patienthood) and psych (cognitive-science and introspection experiments led by its Chief Scientist). Ring core: founded in 2024 with AI welfare as its founding mission, staffed from FHI, CAIS and OpenAI (E). Transfer into_model: its welfare evaluations and interventions target models and how labs treat them (J1); into_institutions is a close second for its advice to labs and policymakers. Problems pair ai_status with assurance because it builds welfare evaluations (F). Framing catastrophic per L (moral catastrophe at scale), though its tone is measured.

name: Rethink Priorities: AI Cognition Initiative (AI Cognition Institute) and Digital Consciousness Model
summary: A research group within Rethink Priorities' Worldview Investigations team, launched as a named initiative in late 2025. Its site calls it the 'AI Cognition Institute', its donation page the 'AI Cognition Initiative'. It studies AI consciousness and moral status, the risk attitudes of agentic AI, and cognitive mechanisms such as introspection and preference coherence. Its flagship is the Digital Consciousness Model, a probabilistic framework combining 13 theoretical perspectives and more than 200 indicators. Initial results (arXiv, January 2026) put the evidence against 2024 LLMs being conscious, though not decisively.
why_it_matters: It brings methods from Rethink Priorities' invertebrate-sentience and moral-weight research to AI, aggregating evidence across rival theories of consciousness instead of choosing one. This gives labs and policymakers a comparable, updatable estimate across AI systems and animals.

key_work.title: Initial results of the Digital Consciousness Model
The Scale of Digital Minds (Derek Shiller)
Risk Alignment in Agentic AI Systems (Clatterbuck, Castro, Muñoz Morán)
From Cacophony to Hierarchy: functional levels of consciousness (with Google DeepMind)

funding: Funded through Rethink Priorities by foundations and individuals; donations via every.org. RP's Nov 2025 appeal put its 2026 core budget at $7.5M, said Worldview Investigations could absorb up to $2M more, and set aside $130K for digital-consciousness policy work. Specific funders of this team are not named.
status_evidence: Sep 2026: revised arXiv version of the Digital Consciousness Model paper; Apr 2026: RP published 'Initial results of the Digital Consciousness Model'
engage: Supervises FIG Fellowship research projects (the fellowship is run by Future Impact Group)
Donations via every.org
caveats: The initiative's name is inconsistent (Initiative versus Institute). The Digital Consciousness Model's outputs depend on expert-chosen theories, indicators and weights. Derek Shiller, a DCM author, is now an adviser here and a senior researcher at Eleos, so the two entries overlap in people. The roster's claim of a Moral Weight Project 2.0 with NYU CMEP was not verified.
tag_notes: Home minds (B13: consciousness indicators and moral-status assessment of AI; sub minds_welfare per the taxonomy example, though minds_science also fits the DCM); secondaries philosophy (staff philosophers, moral weight) and formal (decision theory behind its risk-attitude work). Ring core: a team of an EA research organisation whose primary mission is AI moral status and agentic risk, carrying over methods from animal-sentience research (E1). Transfer into_model: the DCM and risk-attitude benchmarks evaluate AI systems themselves (J1). Org type programme (I: unit inside Rethink Priorities). Region global (O: a remote-first organisation). Way of knowing formal because the flagship output is a Monte Carlo probabilistic model. Status active rather than new, since the named initiative continues Worldview Investigations work from before 2025.

name: Wisdom and Culture Lab (University of Waterloo)
summary: Igor Grossmann's psychology lab at the University of Waterloo studies how people make wise decisions in everyday life, across cultures and over time. Its methods are surveys, behavioural experiments and computational work (modelling, NLP, large-scale analyses). It leads the Wise Judgment Consortium (15 labs on five continents) and co-authored a 2026 Trends in Cognitive Sciences paper arguing that AI needs metacognitive wisdom strategies. In September 2026 it opened two new AI programmes, one on metacognition in advanced AI systems and one on human-AI systems for expert judgement and forecasting.
why_it_matters: It brings the empirical science of wisdom (intellectual humility, perspective-seeking, context adaptation), with cross-cultural ground truth, to AI design and evaluation. That gives 'wise AI' and wisdom evals a measurable psychological basis rather than a purely philosophical one.

key_work.title: Imagining and building wise machines: The centrality of AI metacognition (Trends in Cognitive Sciences)
Wise Judgment Consortium: preregistered 15-lab cross-cultural study of wise judgement
New research programmes on AI metacognition and on human-AI systems for expert judgement and forecasting

people: Igor Grossmann (lab director; Professor of Psychology)
Samuel G. B. Johnson (first author of the 'wise machines' paper)
status_evidence: 29 Sep 2026: posted a postdoctoral fellowship in AI Metacognition and Reasoning, a postdoc in Human-AI Systems for Expert Judgment, and a research project manager role, all for two new AI programmes.
engage: Postdoctoral Research Fellowship in AI Metacognition and Reasoning (CAD 65-70k; review from 15 Oct 2026)
Postdoctoral Fellow in Human-AI Systems for Expert Judgment (posted Sep 2026)
Research Project Manager: AI, Judgment, and Forecasting (posted Sep 2026)
On Wisdom Podcast, co-hosted by Grossmann
caveats: Its AI programmes are new (announced September 2026) and their funders aren't named. Before that, its AI work was mainly the wise-machines position paper. It treats wisdom as cognitive strategies measured from the outside, not as contemplative practice.
tag_notes: Home psych (B2: third-person wisdom research is Psychology; the method is social and cultural psychology plus judgement and decision-making). Secondary democracy: Grossmann founded the Social Science Forecasting Collaborative, and one new programme is on forecasting. Ring bridge (E3): an established psychology lab whose AI work is framed explicitly around safer, more robust AI (the paper cites 'prosaic and catastrophic failures') and is now a standing, staffed programme. Transfer into_model: metacognitive strategies, and evaluations of reasoning under uncertainty, aimed at model behaviour. Problems: values first (wisdom as a design target); assurance paired with it because the lab builds evaluations (F); epistemics for human-AI forecasting.

name: Positive AI Labs
summary: A US nonprofit, set up in 2025, that plans to build open-source datasets and evaluations to steer frontier models towards 'positive alignment': actively supporting human flourishing and pluralistic wisdom rather than only avoiding harm. Its four-stage pipeline (curation, translation, validation, adoption) gathers material from philosophy, ethics and spiritual traditions, including Buddhist teachers, and turns it into training and evaluation data. A board drawn from business and venture capital runs it, with advisers from Meta, Stanford/Google DeepMind and Cambridge.
why_it_matters: It is one of very few groups trying to turn wisdom traditions into concrete, open evaluation and training data for frontier models. That is the 'wisdom evals' gap the harm-prevention focus of mainstream safety mostly leaves open.

key_work.title: Positive Alignment: Artificial Intelligence for Human Flourishing (arXiv preprint; adviser Arun Rao a co-author under a Positive AI Labs affiliation)
Translation Pipeline for wisdom-sourced open datasets and evaluations

people: Stacey Lawson (board member; co-founder of Ygrene Energy Fund)
Lake Dai (board member; Managing Partner, Sancus Ventures)
status_evidence: May 2026: adviser Arun Rao listed with a Positive AI Labs affiliation on the 'Positive Alignment' preprint (revised Jun 2026). The organisation's own site (© 2025) shows no dated outputs.
