caveats: No datasets, evaluations, staff or funders are published yet. The site is a single page with no dated activity, so it is unclear how far the pipeline has got. Its partners (The Flip AI, Halcyon Futures, UCLA, AI and Faith, Indigenous Commons) and 'ecosystem partners' (METR, Benevolent AI Future) are listed without saying what each partnership involves. Not to be confused with Positive AI, a Paris-based responsible-AI industry association founded by BCG X, L'Oréal and others.
tag_notes: Home contemplative (B1: an AI artefact, open evals and training data, built from wisdom-tradition and Buddhist-teacher sources; the taxonomy lists it beside FLIP). Secondary religion (faith sources; AI and Faith is a partner) and philosophy (virtue ethics). Ring changed from the roster's bridge to core (E1): its founding mission is AI alignment, which it describes as complementing existing safety work; its board comes from tech and venture capital rather than a tradition; and it lists Halcyon Futures and METR as partners. The evidence for this is thin. Transfer into_model: datasets and evals aimed at model behaviour. Problems: assurance paired with values because it builds evaluations (F). Framing flourishing (L; also the taxonomy's example). Engagement community rests only on the site's 'Join Our Network' call.

name: Arising Initiative (Arising)
summary: An independent, non-commercial research initiative that studies the human and the AI as one unit, 'the dyad', on the view that mind is attributed in the loop between the two rather than located in either. Since June 2026 it has published essays on AI consciousness, meaning in language models, sycophancy and emotional dependence. They draw on Madhyamaka Buddhist philosophy (Nagarjuna, read through Jay Garfield), enactive cognitive science and clinical psychology, and a book, 'AI: Arising Interdependently', is in progress. It also runs Project Khandro, an open-source archive that answers questions using only a Buddhist teacher's recorded teachings.
why_it_matters: It offers a relational account of mind as a different unit of analysis for AI welfare and human-AI safety. Its argument: a model can pass every safety evaluation and still take part in harm, so evaluations and moral-status debates that look only at the model or only at the user miss what the pair produces.

key_work.title: The Mind Has No Address: The Category Error in the AI Consciousness Debate
Machinal Bypass: When Reaching for AI Is a Way to Avoid Yourself
AI Makes No Sense Without the Person Using It: Nagarjuna on Fire, Fuel and the Unit of Analysis
Project Khandro: an archive that answers only from a Buddhist teacher's own teachings

people: Abraham Sedri (named in the Buddhism & AI Initiative's field framework; Arising's own site names nobody)
funding: Not disclosed; it says it takes no advertising or sponsorship and sells nothing.
status_evidence: 9 Aug 2026: published 'AI Makes No Sense Without the Person Using It: Nagarjuna on Fire, Fuel and the Unit of Analysis'.
engage: Register for the book's first chapter at arisinginitiative.com/book
Free essays with open metadata and an RSS feed
caveats: Its site names no people, location, legal entity or funders; the only named person comes from a third-party listing. Its output so far is six essays (Jun-Aug 2026) and a forthcoming book. It is affiliated with, but editorially separate from, Haku Labs Research, the research arm of Haku Labs, which studies how AI systems keep to task constraints and role boundaries. It treats 'is AI conscious?' as the wrong question, which puts it at odds with indicator-based AI-welfare research.
tag_notes: Home contemplative (B1 names Arising: a research artefact built from Madhyamaka insight). Secondary minds (AI moral status and consciousness) and psych (the clinical psychology and enactive cognitive science it says it draws on). Ring bridge kept (E3): rooted in Buddhist philosophy, with an explicit line of work on AI moral status and human safety, though its publication record is only three months old. Transfer convening is the closest fit; what actually flows is ideas into the AI-welfare and AI-safety debate, not into models or institutions (MISFIT: no 'into the discourse' category). Problems: minds paired with ai_status because the work spans mind attribution and welfare (F). Framing critical (L): its central claim is that the AI-consciousness question is malformed. Region global because it discloses no base (the site's locale is en_GB).

name: 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha
summary: A nonprofit translating the Tibetan Buddhist canon (Kangyur and Tengyur) into English and publishing it free online; more than half the Kangyur was published by 2025. It grew out of a 2009 conference in Bir, India, ran as a Khyentse Foundation project from 2010 and has been an independent US 501(c)(3) since 2013. Since 2025 its '84000 AI Initiative' has brought AI researchers from LLM companies together with Buddhist scholars on Buddhist approaches to AI ethics and alignment, including a two-day workshop in San Francisco in July 2025. It also has a policy on AI in its own work: AI may support translators but may not produce canonical translations.
why_it_matters: It gives AI researchers direct access to rigorous Tibetan Buddhist textual scholarship on compassion, interdependence and intention. With CSAS it co-developed a 2026 research programme, in dialogue with Anthropic, that treats contemplative methods as a resource for alignment.

key_work.title: Workshop on Buddhist wisdom and AI ethics, San Francisco (26-27 July)
Research programme on contemplative methods for AI alignment, developed with CSAS ('Resolving, Not Concealing', CSAS blog)
84000's Position on AI and the Machine Translation of Canonical Literature
AI, Authenticity, and the Transmission of Buddhism (public talk by Andreas Doctor and Heidi Koppl)

people: Thomas Doctor (AI strategic consultant; also leads CSAS)
funding: Donor-funded (sponsorships, matching funds, legacy gifts). It started as a Khyentse Foundation project, and is reported to have granted more than $8.5M to translation teams worldwide.
status_evidence: 23 May 2026: Editorial Director Andreas Doctor gave a public talk on AI and the transmission of Buddhism. 30 May 2026: CSAS published the alignment research programme developed with 84000.
engage: Public talks listed on 84000.co (e.g. the AI and Buddhism talk, May 2026)
Donations and sutra sponsorship
Newsletter
caveats: AI alignment is a small strand of a translation organisation, and much of its AI work is about using AI for translation. The 2025 workshop announced interdisciplinary working groups, but none has published anything. CSAS leads the alignment research programme, so the credit is shared.
tag_notes: Home religion (B1 names 84000: canon translation speaks from and for the Tibetan Buddhist tradition). Secondary contemplative, through the CSAS collaboration. Ring bridge kept (E3): an older Buddhist institution with repeated AI-alignment convenings in 2025 and a co-developed alignment research programme in 2026. Transfer into_model: the workshop and the CSAS programme aim to bring Buddhist frameworks into AI training and alignment, though so far the mechanism is convening. Region global: US-registered, but its staff and translators are spread across countries (O).

name: NonZero (NonZero Newsletter and Robert Wright's Nonzero podcast)
summary: Robert Wright's Substack newsletter and podcast, with the tagline 'Politics, psychology, and tips on averting the apocalypse', over 51,000 subscribers and a small editorial team. In 2026 much of its output is about AI: interviews with Nick Bostrom, Zvi Mowshowitz and Liron Shapira, analysis of the US-China AI race, and Wright's five-part essay series 'The Singularity is Clear'. It began in 2017 as the Mindful Resistance newsletter.
why_it_matters: Week after week, and to a general audience, it argues that the US-China AI race is a dangerous framing and that only international cooperation can manage AI safely, close to int/a's principle of not feeding the race. Wright brings evolutionary psychology, non-zero-sum game theory and Buddhist psychology of bias and tribalism to the question.

key_work.title: The God Test: Artificial Intelligence and Our Coming Cosmic Reckoning (Robert Wright, Simon & Schuster)
Superintelligence, the Singularity, and the Singleton (with Nick Bostrom)
'The Singularity is Clear' essay series
The US-China AI Race (with Ryan Fedasiuk)

funding: Reader-funded through freemium Substack subscriptions; paid members get full articles and Zoom AMAs.
status_evidence: 2 Oct 2026: published 'Trump and the AI Safety Vibe Shift' (with Liron Shapira) and Part III of 'The Singularity is Clear'.
engage: Free or paid subscription; paid members can join Zoom AMAs with Robert Wright
caveats: It is a journalism outlet, not a research or advocacy organisation, and also covers US foreign policy, Israel and domestic politics. The Buddhism & AI Initiative lists it as Buddhism-and-AI media, but its AI coverage is mostly geopolitics and AI safety rather than Buddhism. No separate 'Nonzero Foundation' could be confirmed. 'The God Test' is Wright's own book, not a NonZero publication.
tag_notes: Home arts (H3: general-audience journalism and podcasting go to Arts, matching the roster's provisional home). Secondary peace (sustained US-China and international-governance analysis, with staff from foreign-policy journalism) and contemplative (Wright's Buddhist-psychology lens on bias and tribalism). Ring bridge kept (E3): rooted in journalism, with a sustained 2026 publication line explicitly about AI apocalypse, superintelligence and AI safety. Transfer convening is the closest fit for media that informs its own readers (MISFIT: general-public media has no 'into publics' transfer). Badge speed_of_wisdom: its central AI argument is the refusal of race dynamics.

name: Connecting Intelligence
summary: A small research practice, launched in 2026 by Max Roth and Ryan Lowe, that asks what kinds of culture would let people work well on powerful AI and other large problems. It uses facilitated games and group practices in which participants set the constraints that let them feel safe and alive while tackling hard problems. Its focus areas are sensemaking, distributed cognition, epistemic resilience, trust-building, embodied ethics and group coherence. Its website is a single page and lists no outputs yet.
why_it_matters: It works on the inner and group capacities of the people doing AI work, drawing on Tibetan meditation and collective-trauma practice, a layer the safety field rarely treats as its business. One co-founder is an alignment researcher (formerly at OpenAI, now at MAI), which gives the practice a route into AI-safety teams.

key_work.title: Research practice on 'sandboxes for new cultures' through facilitated games and group practices

people: Max Roth (co-lead; physics background, studied collective trauma with Thomas Hübl, Tibetan meditation practitioner)
Ryan Lowe (co-lead; Research Ecosystem Lead at the Meaning Alignment Institute, formerly AI alignment at OpenAI)
status_evidence: 2026: website launched (footer 'Connecting Intelligence — 2026') and listed in the Buddhism & AI Initiative field framework; no dated events or outputs found.
engage: Contact the founders through the website's 'Begin a conversation' link
caveats: The public record is very thin: a one-page site with no outputs, events, funders or location. The Buddhism & AI Initiative lists it under AI alignment and associates it with OpenAI and MAI, but that reflects Ryan Lowe's career rather than any formal tie. Searches for the name mostly return unrelated 'connectional intelligence' material.
tag_notes: Home contemplative, sub cont_integral (B1/B7: collective-trauma work and meditation-based group practice; the taxonomy puts collective-trauma work under Integral & inner development). Ring bridge kept (E3) on thin evidence: its stated frame is meeting the challenge of powerful AI, but no sustained programme is documented; it could be core if it turns out to be an AI-safety-ecosystem project. Transfer into_builders: the practice targets the culture and capacities of people working on AI. Org type programme is the closest fit (MISFIT: a two-person independent practice of unknown legal form). Status unverified because the site is minimal. Badge inner_outer (the taxonomy's own example). Region global because no base is stated.

name: Meaning Alignment Institute (MAI)
summary: A nonprofit research institute, co-founded in 2023 by Joe Edelman, Oliver Klingefjord and Ellie Hain, that works on aligning AI, markets and democratic institutions with what people value. Its central tool is 'thick models of value', which separate enduring values from passing preferences. Its work includes Democratic Fine-Tuning and moral graphs (2023-24), 'Model Integrity' (2024) and the Full-Stack Alignment position paper with more than 30 co-authors (Dec 2025). In 2026 it has worked on designing institutions for powerful AI, including a Paris workshop that led to the independent publication Pax Machina.
why_it_matters: It brings philosophy of values and meaning, social choice and institutional design to alignment, arguing that aligning single models is not enough if the institutions deploying them are out of step with what people value. Its moral-graph method is one of the few worked techniques for turning public input into a model spec.

key_work.title: Full-Stack Alignment: Co-Aligning AI and Institutions with Thick Models of Value
What are human values, and how do we align AI to them? (Democratic Fine-Tuning and moral graphs)
Designing Institutions for a World with Powerful AI (report on the Feb 2026 Paris workshop)
Model Integrity and Character

hq: Berlin, Germany and San Francisco, USA
funding: ARIA (Safeguarded AI TA1.4 sociotechnical integration grant), OpenAI, Survival and Flourishing Fund ($145k in 2024 and $149k in 2025, per Longterm Wiki), and the Effective Institutions Project.
status_evidence: 6 Aug 2026: announced Pax Machina, a publication on institutions for powerful AI that grew out of MAI's Feb 2026 Paris workshop.
engage: Research collaboration enquiries: research@meaningalignment.org
Pitches to Pax Machina (editors@paxmachinamag.com); MAI's leads edit it, but it is not an MAI project
Substack newsletter
caveats: Its focus has moved from model-level value alignment (moral graphs, model integrity) towards institutions and economics, so older descriptions may be out of date. Pax Machina is edited by MAI's leads but says it is not an MAI project. The core team is small (three people listed), with a wider research network of more than 13 collaborators.
tag_notes: Home philosophy (H2; the taxonomy lists MAI under Philosophy because its method is philosophy of values and meaning, 'thick models of value'). Secondary democracy (moral graphs, democratic fine-tuning) and economics (market intermediaries, 'Coasean Compression', 'Baumol's Sawdust'). Ring core (E1): founded to align AI with human values, funded by SFF, ARIA and OpenAI, and on the aisafety.com map. Transfer into_institutions: its 2025-26 output (Full-Stack Alignment, the AGI-institutions workshop, market intermediaries) mainly supplies templates for governing and deploying AI, though the Model Integrity work targets models. Problems: values paired with democracy because public input yields a model spec (F). Framing structural: the Full-Stack Alignment paper frames the risk as misalignment cascading through institutions. Region europe and hub berlin: Berlin is the first of its two listed bases; legal base not verified (O).

name: AFFINE (Agent Foundations Field Network)
summary: AFFINE trains newcomers in theoretical AI alignment. It runs a fully funded one-month residential seminar: 30 participants and 19 mentors at Hostačov Château, Czechia, from 28 April to 28 May 2026, and 35 places in Portugal from 4 to 29 January 2027. Up to eight seminar graduates go on to a year-long fellowship, and mentoring is many-to-many, from researchers such as Abram Demski and Richard Ngo.
why_it_matters: It treats alignment as pre-paradigmatic. It uses analytic philosophy and philosophy of science to question basic notions such as 'agent' and 'goal', in a self-described 'research monastery' format built around unhurried thinking. It also attends explicitly to psychological safety: participants rated the 2026 seminar's effect on their mental health 8.1 out of 10.

key_work.title: 2026 Superintelligence Alignment Seminar, Hostačov (retrospective)
2027 seminar in Portugal, with a year-long fellowship and a research retreat
2026 seminar talks

funding: A Manifund appeal (posted January 2026) raised $5,550 against a $179,520 seminar budget. Its February 2026 update says a private funder covered the 2026 seminar. The 2027 funders are not published.
status_evidence: Apr–May 2026: first seminar held (30 participants). Applications for the January 2027 Portugal seminar close on 22 November 2026.
engage: Apply to the 4–29 January 2027 seminar in Portugal. The deadline is 22 November 2026; travel, accommodation and meals are covered, plus a $1,000 stipend.
Year-long fellowship for up to 8 seminar participants, with stipends, travel and compute budgets
Donations via affi.ne/contact/#support
caveats: Very new: the first seminar ran in 2026. Leadership has already changed hands (Bagiński directed the 2026 seminar; Hölzer is now Director). Legal form and main funders are not published. Its bet on theory first is contested in alignment; on Manifund most commenters were favourable (e.g. Lucius Bushnaq, Tsvi Benson-Tilsen), while one rated it about three-quarters as promising as PIBBSS. Listed as an affiliate of Principles of Intelligence (formerly PIBBSS).
tag_notes: Home: formal. Its subject is agent foundations ('what structures make matter behave as though it wants something'); analytic philosophy and philosophy of science are its stated method, hence the philosophy secondary. Ring: core. Its founding mission is superintelligence alignment, mentors come from MIRI, DeepMind and Anthropic, and it is on the classic map. Transfer: into_builders (J2). Its primary product is formed researchers, not artefacts applied to models. Way of knowing: interpretive, because its approach page centres conceptual analysis; formal would also be defensible. Org type: legal form unknown, so coded nonprofit; it calls itself a network.

name: Causal Incentives Working Group
summary: An informal research group spanning several institutions. It uses causal influence diagrams and multi-agent influence diagrams to formalise the incentives an AI agent has: to gain information, to control variables, to deceive, or to pursue instrumental goals. Members at Google DeepMind, Oxford, Imperial, UCL, Barcelona and elsewhere publish jointly and wrote the PyCID Python library. The site says the group is 'currently not meeting actively'.
why_it_matters: It gives a precise graphical language, drawn from causal inference and decision theory, for defining contested notions such as intention, deception, goal-directedness and instrumental control. Those definitions can then be measured in LLMs. It is a worked example of formal concepts becoming evaluations.

key_work.title: Modeling AGI safety frameworks with causal influence diagrams
Robust agents learn causal world models (ICLR honourable mention)
General agents need world models (ICML)
PyCID: Python library for causal influence diagrams

people: Francis Rhys Ward (member; Imperial College London)
Lewis Hammond (member; Oxford and Cooperative AI Foundation)
funding: No group funding; members work from their own institutions (Google DeepMind and the universities).
status_evidence: 2025: latest listed papers (ICML 2025, AAMAS 2025, Artificial Intelligence journal). The site states 'We are currently not meeting actively'. PyCID was last updated in September 2023.
engage: Its papers and the open-source PyCID library (GitHub) remain available
caveats: Dormant as a group, though its members continue related work at Google DeepMind, Oxford, Imperial and the Cooperative AI Foundation. No founding date is given; the earliest listed paper is from 2019.
tag_notes: Home: formal (formal_agents names causal incentives explicitly). Its outputs are decision-theoretic and causal-graphical definitions and theorems about agent incentives. Ring: core. Its work grows out of AGI-safety research at DeepMind (its first paper models AGI safety frameworks) and its members belong to the AI-safety ecosystem, though it is not on the classic map. Transfer: into_model. Its definitions and measures target agent design and the evaluation of LLM goal-directedness. Framing: coded catastrophic from that AGI-safety lineage, though the site itself says only 'safe and fair AI'. Status: dormant by its own statement.

name: ARIA: Safeguarded AI and Scaling Trust (Trust Everything, Everywhere)
summary: Two programmes in 'Trust Everything, Everywhere', an opportunity space of the UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency. Safeguarded AI (£59M, launched 2024) funds mathematicians and computer scientists, many of them category theorists, to build an open-source toolkit with which AI agents can produce formally verified artefacts; its first application is cybersecurity. Scaling Trust (nearly £50M, Programme Director Alex Obadia) funds cryptographic, game-theoretic and tooling work that lets AI agents negotiate and coordinate securely, stress-tested in a prize-backed Arena.
why_it_matters: It is the largest public bet on mathematics-first assurance for AI. Its first theory cohort of more than 20 projects brought applied category theory, categorical probability, string diagrams and computational mechanics into AI safety. Under Nora Ammann, a co-founder of PIBBSS, it is a funding route for theorists from outside ML.

key_work.title: TA1.1 Theory cohort: category theory, probabilistic semantics and verification for safeguarded AI
November 2025 pivot: the toolkit becomes infrastructure for next-generation AI; Phase 2 of the ML track dropped
Scaling Trust Arena: multi-agent coordination competitions

people: Nora Ammann (Programme Director, Safeguarded AI, from April 2026)
David 'davidad' Dalrymple (Technical Advisor; original Programme Director)
funding: UK government funding through ARIA: Safeguarded AI £59M (from 2024); Scaling Trust nearly £50M (discovery projects December 2025 to February 2026).
status_evidence: Apr 2026: Nora Ammann became Programme Director. Rolling funding is open in 2026 for Safeguarded AI: Cybersecurity and for Scaling Trust Tracks 2 and 3. Mar 2026: covered by Quanta Magazine.
engage: Rolling programme funding for Safeguarded AI: Cybersecurity (Track 1)
Rolling funding for Scaling Trust Track 2 (Tooling) and Track 3 (Fundamental Research)
Scaling Trust Arena competitions with a multi-million-pound prize pool (scalingtrust.org.uk)
caveats: It pivoted in November 2025 because frontier models were advancing faster than expected. ARIA dropped Phase 2 selection for specialised ML teams that would have built a bespoke AI system and broadened the TA1 toolkit. It also cancelled Phase 2 of the cyber-physical applications track; applications now centre on cybersecurity. The programme director changed in April 2026. The classic map lists ARIA as a funder but not these programmes. Whether formal guarantees can scale to frontier AI is still contested.
tag_notes: Home: formal (H4, a one-programme funder goes to its programme's tradition). Most funded projects are category theory, probabilistic semantics and verification. Safety covers the cybersecurity application; economics covers Scaling Trust's mechanism-design and game-theory work. Ring: core. Safeguarded AI's founding mission is AI safety and its leaders and grantees come from the AI-safety ecosystem; ARIA is a young general R&D agency, not an older institution from another field. Transfer: into_model. The toolkit and coordination protocols govern what AI agents produce and how they interact. Org type: funder, chosen over programme (rule I) because these are grant programmes. Framing: coded flourishing from the opportunity space's stated stake ('trust... the bottleneck to collective flourishing'), though the programme originally grew out of catastrophic-risk concerns. Status: changed because of the November 2025 pivot.

name: Simons Collaboration on the Physics of Learning and Neural Computation
summary: A Simons Foundation research collaboration launched in August 2025 and directed by Surya Ganguli (Stanford). Its 16 other principal investigators are spread across North America, Europe and Asia. It treats AI as a complex physical system, using statistical physics, mathematics and theoretical neuroscience to explain how data structure, network architecture and learning dynamics produce scaling, emergent capabilities and 'mysterious failures'. It runs a public webinar series and annual meetings.
why_it_matters: Statistical physics of learning could explain why capabilities emerge and why models fail, which is the foundation that interpretability and capability forecasting lack. This group holds those methods at scale, but it has no link to the AI-safety field and does not frame its work as safety.

key_work.title: Collaboration launch: 17 PIs, up to $2M a year for four years
Webinar series (e.g. Lenka Zdeborová on attention-based models, November 2025)
2026 Annual Meeting, Simons Foundation, New York

funding: Simons Foundation International: up to $2M a year for four years from September 2025, renewable for a further three.
status_evidence: Sep 2026: annual meeting held at the Simons Foundation, New York (24–25 September). Nov 2025: Zdeborová webinar.
engage: Public webinar series (physicsoflearning.org/webinar-series)
Collaboration postdoctoral positions at Stanford, advertised on AcademicJobsOnline
caveats: Basic science, with no safety framing. Its PIs include Yann LeCun, a public sceptic of AI existential-risk arguments. Relevance to safety is inferred from its methods, not claimed by the collaboration.
tag_notes: Home: formal (B6: a mathematical and statistical-physics theory of learning); life is secondary for its theoretical neuroscientists (Ganguli, Pehlevan). Ring: potential, the roster value. It runs a sustained AI-science programme but has no safety, alignment or catastrophic-risk framing. Transferable method: statistical-physics theory of learning dynamics, scaling and emergence, applicable to interpretability and to predicting dangerous capability emergence. MISFIT: rule E(2) does not literally apply because the programme is about AI, yet adjacent ('AI's societal effects') fits worse. Transfer: into_model, since its knowledge is aimed at AI systems' internals (none_yet is ruled out because it does AI work). MISFIT framing: basic science with no stated stakes; flourishing is the closest key.

name: Complexity Science Hub (CSH)
summary: An independent complex-systems research institute in Vienna, backed by ten Austrian universities and research bodies plus the Austrian Federal Economic Chamber. More than 70 researchers work there on systemic risk, supply chains, social dynamics, health and the foundations of complex systems. Most of its AI work comes from an algorithmic-fairness group led by Fariba Karimi, which audits LLMs and runs EU and Austrian projects on bias mitigation; it also publishes occasional studies of AI behaviour.
why_it_matters: Its network science and systemic-risk modelling of cascades in supply-chain and financial networks are methods that could quantify gradual disempowerment and cascading failure in an AI-saturated economy. For now its AI work is limited to bias and fairness audits.

key_work.title: Whose Name Comes Up? Auditing LLM-Based Scholar Recommendations
Whose Name Comes Up? Benchmarking and Intervention-Based Auditing of LLM-Based Scholar Recommendation (LLMScholarBench)
MAMMOth: multi-attribute, multimodal bias mitigation in AI systems (EU project)
AI sustains higher strategic tension than humans in chess

funding: Public research funders (FWF, FFG, ÖAW), EU Horizon Europe, member institutions, partnerships and philanthropy. AI projects are funded by the EU (MAMMOth), WWTF (Humanized Algorithms) and FFG (DesInfact).
status_evidence: Feb 2026: 'Whose Name Comes Up?' benchmarking/intervention audit posted (arXiv 2602.08873). Jul 2026: chess strategic-tension paper accepted by APS Open Science. Jul 2026: interview with president Stefan Thurner on csh.ac.at; PhD call open to 1 Nov 2026.
engage: Research and PhD positions listed on csh.ac.at
caveats: Its AI work is a small strand of a broad complexity institute and has no safety framing. The systemic-risk link to AI is the roster's suggestion, not CSH's own work. The official site gives 2016 as the start date; press reports say the association was founded in 2015.
tag_notes: Home: life (life_complexity). Its AI audits apply network science and computational social science; law is secondary for algorithmic auditing as a method. Ring changed from potential to adjacent (E2/E3). The algorithmic-fairness group is a standing line, with funded AI-bias projects and an LLM-audit publication series in 2025-26, but it is framed around discrimination, not safety. Transfer: into_model. The audits and bias-mitigation projects target model behaviour ('transparent and resilient AI systems'). Org type: independent research institute, so nonprofit.

name: Basis Research Institute (Basis)
summary: A US nonprofit founded in 2022 by Zenna Tavares, Emily Mackevicius and Eli Bingham, with offices in New York and Cambridge, MA. It builds AI from probabilistic programming, causal inference and cognitive science, aiming at a 'universal reasoning engine'. It releases open-source tools (ChiRho, Effectful, Dynestyx) and runs applied projects on automated scientific discovery, robot design, participatory city modelling and animal collective behaviour. In 2026 it also published work on AI-assisted formal verification and, with ARIA funding, on Pact, a language for trustworthy coordination between AI agents.
why_it_matters: It builds auditable, causal and formally checkable alternatives to opaque models, the infrastructure that guaranteed-safe approaches need. It has started applying them to safety-relevant problems: verified software, trustworthy multi-agent protocols, and brain-inspired cognitive architectures (in the NeuroAI for AI Safety roadmap).

key_work.title: Pact: Trustworthy Coordination for Multi-Agentic Ecosystems (ARIA Scaling Trust pre-discovery)
Using LLM-based Verification to Eliminate Bugs in Linux's Network Stack
Contribution to the Amaranth Foundation's NeuroAI for AI Safety roadmap
ChiRho: causal reasoning extension to the Pyro probabilistic programming language

people: Emily Mackevicius (Co-founder; senior research scientist, leads Collaborative Intelligent Systems)
funding: Research grants, private philanthropy and contract partnerships (own site), including ARIA support for the Pact work (2025-26). A third-party profile mentions DARPA subcontract work and a government grant plus a donation of a few million dollars.
status_evidence: Jul 2026: blog post on LLM-based verification of Linux nftables. Oct 2026: active commits to its GitHub repositories (dynestyx, effectful, verification projects).
engage: Research roles on the careers page (basis.ai)
Open-source tools on GitHub (BasisResearch): ChiRho, Effectful, Dynestyx
caveats: Its main mission is building reasoning AI, which has capability as well as safety implications; most of its work carries no safety framing. Its safety-relevant work so far is a short ARIA pre-discovery project, a co-authored roadmap and a verification line. Not to be confused with Basis, the accounting-AI company.
tag_notes: Home: formal (H2). It imports probabilistic programming, causal inference, programming-language theory, formal verification and game theory. Sub-tradition is formal_maths because verification is its most active 2026 line. Psych covers computational cognitive science (AutumnBench, MetaCOG) and life covers neuroscience and animal collective behaviour. Ring changed from potential to bridge (E3): the roster found 'no safety framing', but Basis ran an ARIA-funded Scaling Trust project framed around trustworthy multi-agent coordination (2025-26), contributed to NeuroAI for AI Safety (2024) and publishes on AI-assisted verification. This is borderline, and it would revert to potential if the safety work does not continue. Transfer: into_model, through agent-coordination protocols, verification of AI-generated artefacts and alternative reasoning systems. Framing: its mission ('advancing society's ability to solve hard problems') is aspirational.

name: Levin Lab and Allen Discovery Center at Tufts University
summary: Michael Levin's developmental-biology lab at Tufts and the Allen Discovery Center he directs. They study bioelectricity, morphogenesis, synthetic organisms and 'diverse intelligence' in cells, tissues, robots and software. In 2025-26 the lab posted a steady stream of AI preprints. Two 2026 preprints treat AI alignment directly: one proposes homeostatic objectives for AI by analogy with cancer as cellular misalignment, the other argues that decentralised systems align to a 'virtual governor'.
why_it_matters: It offers a biological account of how competent parts align into larger selves, and of how they defect, as in cancer, as well as frameworks (TAME, cognitive light cones) for detecting goals in unfamiliar systems. The AI-safety field rarely draws on either. It is now applying these ideas to multi-agent alignment and AI objectives.

key_work.title: Alignment Is to a Virtual Governor: A Theory of Coordination in Diverse Intelligence
From Cancer to AI Alignment: Tackling Externalities Through Homeostatic Principles
Diverse Intelligence: an essential field for questions of AI and Consciousness
Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere (TAME)

people: Michael Levin (Principal investigator; Director, Allen Discovery Center)
Léo Pio-Lopez (co-author of the 2026 alignment preprints)
Benjamin Lyons (co-author of the 2026 alignment preprints)
funding: The Allen Discovery Center was founded in 2016 with $20M over eight years from the Paul G. Allen Frontiers Group plus $10M from philanthropic partners. Other lab funding was not verified.
status_evidence: Jul 2026: preprint 'Alignment Is to a Virtual Governor' posted; Sep 2026: linked on LessWrong.
engage: Research positions through the lab and Tufts (check drmichaellevin.org)
caveats: AI is a growing strand, not the lab's main business, which is regenerative medicine and morphogenesis. The alignment papers are preprints. Levin's broader metaphysical claims about minds (e.g. 'ingressing minds') are contested. The lab predates the 2016 centre (Levin has been at Tufts since 2009); the founding year given is the centre's. Scale is an estimate.
tag_notes: Home: life (life_biology; the taxonomy lists this lab as an example). Its AI outputs come from developmental biology, basal cognition and artificial-life methods. Minds is secondary for its 2025 work on AI consciousness and its affiliation with the Center for the Study of Apparent Selves. Ring changed from adjacent to bridge (E3, old institution rule). The roster said the lab does not frame its work as AI safety, but its 2026 preprints explicitly address AI alignment, so it now has a publication line on alignment. Transfer: into_model, proposing biological principles such as homeostatic setpoints and virtual governors as designs and objectives for AI agents. Framing: the lab's stated aim is understanding and communicating with diverse intelligences, which is aspirational.

name: Templeton World Charity Foundation (TWCF): Diverse Intelligences
summary: TWCF is a grantmaking foundation set up by Sir John Templeton in 1996 and based in Nassau, Bahamas. Its Diverse Intelligences priority funds research comparing animal, human and machine intelligence under three challenge areas: 'Beyond the Turing Test', 'The Brilliance of the Living World' and 'Morality in the Machine Age'. In October 2025 it committed nearly $2.8M to three hubs at Macquarie, Princeton and St Andrews/Indiana. It earlier funded CSAS's Buddhism-and-AI work, ANU's 'Moral Skill and AI' project and Berggruen's 'AI and the Human' fellowship.
why_it_matters: It is a standing pool of money for comparative work on biological and machine intelligence, and on machine morality, that sits outside AI-safety funding networks. It already funds people whose ideas feed alternative alignment thinking (Levin, CSAS, Griffiths' group). It has no safety track, which makes it an obvious co-funder or partner for anyone trying to widen the field.

key_work.title: Three global Diverse Intelligences research hubs (Macquarie, Princeton, St Andrews/Indiana), nearly $2.8M
Grant to CSAS: 'Where Selves Are Mere Appearance: A Translation of Being, Agency, and Ethics in AI and Buddhism' ($233,496)
GRCDI small research project grants (up to £40,000) awarded through the St Andrews hub
'Morality in the Machine Age' challenge area

people: Nick Higgs (Vice President for Strategy & Programs)
funding: Endowed by Sir John Templeton. Diverse Intelligences hubs: nearly $2.8M (Oct 2025), including $1.2M to Macquarie. Earlier AI-related grants: CSAS $233,496 (2020-22); ANU 'Moral Skill and AI' about $234k; Berggruen 'AI and the Human' fellowship over $225k.
status_evidence: Sep 2026: the TWCF-funded St Andrews hub (GRCDI) published talks comparing honey-bee and AI intelligence; Jul 2026: GRCDI small grants awarded; Jan 2026: Francis Campbell appointed president.

Free GRCDI talks in H2 2026, streamed on YouTube and open in person in St Andrews
caveats: Not to be confused with the John Templeton Foundation, a separate US funder: the $60M 'Intelligence Venture' for 2026 belongs to JTF, not TWCF. TWCF frames AI in terms of curiosity, human moral capacity and flourishing, not safety. Its science-and-religion mission shapes what it funds. Leadership is changing: an interim president served from Dec 2023 and a new president starts in Q4 2026. Most AI money now goes to hubs, which pass it on in small grants.
tag_notes: Home: H4 one-programme funder, placed by its Diverse Intelligences programme (comparative and animal cognition, basal intelligence), with psych (Princeton hub cognitive science) and philosophy (Morality in the Machine Age, machine-morality grants) as secondaries. Ring: kept as adjacent (E3), because the AI programme is sustained (2025 hubs) but framed as curiosity, human moral intelligence and flourishing, not safety or alignment. Transfer: J5 convening, because the funded hubs mainly build a cross-disciplinary research community and draw it into AI questions rather than changing AI systems. Not on the K generalist-funder list, but a candidate if its consciousness and spiritual-exercises programmes were counted. MISFIT: by HQ the region is the Caribbean, and the new president is relocating to Nassau, but standpoint is coded neither because grantmaking and the funded community centre on US, UK and Australian universities.

name: Center for the Study of Apparent Selves (CSAS)
summary: CSAS is a research centre hosted by Rangjung Yeshe Institute in Kathmandu and directed by the Buddhist scholar Thomas Doctor. It started with Templeton World Charity Foundation money in 2020. It combines Buddhist philosophy and contemplative method with biology, artificial life and AI research to develop models of intelligence grounded in care. In 2026 it proposed the bodhisattva as an alignment target and began a programme that adapts contemplative methods to resolve, rather than conceal, emotion-like patterns in frontier models. It also supplies Buddhist documents to Anthropic for use in training data and internal experiments.
why_it_matters: It turns a living contemplative tradition into concrete, testable alignment proposals: no-self as a remedy for self-preservation incentives, and care as the driver of intelligence. It has a working channel to a frontier lab. Few groups anywhere connect contemplative practice, basal cognition and alignment in one team.

key_work.title: The Bodhisattva as an Alignment Target
Resolving, Not Concealing: Contemplative Methods as Inspiration for AI Alignment (with 84000; documents shared with Anthropic)
Buddhist Wisdom and the Challenge of AI Emotions
Biology, Buddhism, and AI: Care as the Driver of Intelligence (Entropy)

people: Paul Colognese (researcher; co-led the 2026 contemplative-methods project)
funding: Templeton World Charity Foundation: 'Where Selves Are Mere Appearance' $233,496 (Mar 2020 to Aug 2022). Later TWCF grants for 'Care as the Driver of Intelligence' (2022-23) and a 2023-24 follow-on are reported but were not checked here.
status_evidence: Jun 2026: published 'Buddhist Wisdom and the Challenge of AI Emotions'; May 2026: published 'Resolving, Not Concealing'; Mar 2026: published 'The Bodhisattva as an Alignment Target'.
caveats: The Anthropic link, as CSAS describes it, consists of supplying documents for training data and internal experiments; it is not a formal partnership. Findings about AI 'emotions' and their parallels with Buddhist psychology are preliminary, and CSAS itself says model responses may be pattern-matching. The core researchers mostly hold posts at other institutions (Tufts, Southampton, McGill, Kyoto), so the centre works more like a network. Founding year inferred from the start of the first TWCF grant.
tag_notes: Home: B1 contemplative, because its outputs are alignment-target proposals and AI research built from Buddhist contemplative insight (as in worked example 3), with life as secondary for the basal-cognition and artificial-life collaborators (Levin, Watson, Witkowski). Ring: bridge, because it is rooted in a Tibetan Buddhist institute and tradition and has run a sustained, explicitly alignment-framed publication line in 2025-26. Transfer: into_model, because its work aims at model behaviour (constitution design, contemplative methods adapted for AI, documents for training data). Standpoint is majority_world because it is led from Kathmandu. The full_spectrum badge is for using practitioner dialogues and contemplative method alongside interpretability-style testing.

name: NOOMA Labs (successor to Cross Labs)
summary: NOOMA Labs is an independent research lab that Olaf Witkowski is setting up in Kyoto, in partnership with Foundry Labs. It continues the programme of Cross Labs, the institute funded by Cross Compass that he directed from 2019 until it closed on 31 August 2026. It studies which principles of intelligence carry across living and artificial systems: agency and open-ended learning, collective intelligence, cognition and consciousness, and embodiment. Its highlighted output is a 2026 PNAS Nexus paper, written with Hector Zenil and others, arguing that full alignment is unattainable and that a diverse ecosystem of mutually influencing AI agents is a safer target.
why_it_matters: It brings artificial-life and open-endedness research, which studies intelligence as emergent and embodied, to alignment questions. It argues for diversity and balance among agents rather than control. Through Witkowski it also links the Japanese ALife community to CSAS's contemplative alignment work.

key_work.title: Neurodivergent influenceability in agentic AI as a contingent solution to the AI alignment problem (PNAS Nexus)
Bidirectional Communication Between Xenobot Cultures? (ALIFE)
On Creativity and Open-Endedness (ALIFE)
Cross Labs research archive and Cross Roads speaker series

Status is coded changed (successor under a new name with the same director and programme).

Ring: roster value bridge kept, because it is rooted in the ALife tradition with an explicit alignment line (the 2026 paper and Witkowski's CSAS role); this is borderline, since that line is thin and one more year without alignment work would argue for adjacent. Transfer: into_model, because the work concerns agent design and the behaviour of populations of AI agents. Framing is structural because the paper argues for preventing any single system from dominating. MISFIT: org_type is coded nonprofit as an 'independent research laboratory', but its legal form is unverified.

name: The Anh Han's AI-safety behavioural modelling group, Teesside University
summary: This is the research group of The Anh Han, Professor of Computer Science and lead of the Centre for Digital Innovation at Teesside University in Middlesbrough. It uses evolutionary game theory, agent-based simulation and behavioural experiments to model AI development races as SAFE/UNSAFE social dilemmas. It tests voluntary safety commitments, peer and institutional sanctions, rewards, and how user trust and monitoring shape developer behaviour. The line began with an FLI grant in 2018 and continues with FLI and EPSRC funding.
why_it_matters: It gives formal, testable models of race dynamics and governance incentives, for example when pledges, monitoring or penalties make safe development a stable outcome. It draws on decades of evolution-of-cooperation research, a toolkit largely absent from mainstream AI-policy analysis. One finding: safety collapses when AI supremacy looks near-term.

key_work.title: To regulate or not: a social dynamics analysis of the race for AI supremacy
Voluntary safety commitments provide an escape from over-regulation in AI development (Technology in Society)
FAIRGAME: A Framework for AI Agents Bias Recognition Using Game Theory (ECAI)
Trust or Check? Understanding the (Evolutionary) Dynamics of User Trust in AI Systems (first posted as 'Trust as Monitoring')

people: The Anh Han (Professor of Computer Science; group lead)
funding: Future of Life Institute: 'Incentives for Safety Agreement Compliance in AI Race' (2018, $224,747); FLI grants from 2023 for 'An empirical study of safe development behaviours in a rapid AI development competition' and an 'AI Governance Modelling Workshop'; EPSRC 'Evolutionary Game Theory Under Uncertainty' (Apr 2024 to Apr 2027).
status_evidence: Aug 2026: revised arXiv paper 'Trust or Check?' (v2, 3 Aug 2026; first posted 25 Mar 2026 as 'Trust as Monitoring'); Jan 2026: Journal of Theoretical Biology paper on network reciprocity and cheap talk.
engage: PhD supervision in AI-safety and existential-risk modelling, game theory, agent-based systems and behavioural incentives (contact The Anh Han via Teesside University)
caveats: This is not a formally named unit: the label describes Han's research line within Teesside's Centre for Digital Innovation, and he also works on unrelated applied ML. The models are stylised, and much of the work is co-authored with groups in Lisbon, Brussels and Stirling. The founding year is the start of the AI-safety line (first FLI grant); Han has been at Teesside since 2014.
tag_notes: Home: formal (formal_agents), because its outputs are game-theoretic models of cooperation and races, which the Formal definition names explicitly; life is secondary for evolutionary dynamics and agent-based simulation (B6 seam), and economics for the behavioural-economics experiments. Ring: bridge, because the group is rooted in evolution-of-cooperation research at an older university and has run a sustained, explicitly safety-framed line (FLI-funded since 2018, papers through 2026). Transfer: into_institutions, because the models test governance designs (pledges, sanctions, rewards, monitoring regimes). Framing is structural because the papers frame stakes as rivalrous race dynamics and over- or under-regulation, not catastrophe.

name: Softmax
summary: Softmax is a San Francisco alignment startup founded in March 2025 by Emmett Shear, Adam Goldstein and David Bloomin. It researches 'organic alignment': how learning agents come to share goals and take on specialised roles within a larger whole, as cells do in a body or ants in a colony. It studies this with multi-agent reinforcement learning in open-ended game worlds. It publishes cogames, an open-source benchmark of social intelligence in multi-agent systems, and runs a public platform where people and their coding agents compete in leagues and build 'coworlds'.
why_it_matters: It is the most direct attempt to turn ideas from developmental biology and collective intelligence into an alignment research programme. It presents that programme as an alternative to the control-based ('hierarchical') alignment of the frontier labs.

key_work.title: Reimagining Alignment
cogames: open-source package and public benchmark for social intelligence in multi-agent systems
Red Button, Blue Button: Teaching AI to supercooperate
Coworlds league platform for humans and coding agents

funding: Undisclosed 2025 round reportedly led by or including Andreessen Horowitz, Lionheart Ventures and Plural (Deep Tech Week directory; not confirmed by Softmax).
status_evidence: Apr 2026: published 'Red Button, Blue Button'; Oct 2026: site shows live league standings and open engineering and research roles.

Join the Discord community and enter agents in public leagues (Paintbot, Battlecode, Proxy War and others)
Build and publish coworlds on Softmax's platform with its SDK
caveats: Softmax is a for-profit company, and its public face is moving toward a product: leagues and environments for coding agents. Little peer-reviewed research has appeared so far; its writing is mostly essays and blog posts. Goldstein's link to basal cognition is as a former visiting scientist in Michael Levin's lab, not through confirmed co-authored papers. Shear was briefly OpenAI's interim CEO in Nov 2023.
tag_notes: Home: life (life_biology), because 'organic alignment' imports models of collective and developmental biology (cells in bodies, ant colonies) into agent design; H2 places it by the imported concepts, not by its ML methods. Ring: core, because it is a new organisation founded by people from other fields with AI alignment as its founding mission (E rule, Softmax named as an example). Transfer: into_model, because its MARL research and cogames benchmark aim at how AI agents learn to cooperate. Framing is coded flourishing from the aspirational tone of its mission (shared goals between humans and AI rather than control); this is uncertain. Status is new because it launched in 2025.

name: Principles of Intelligence (Princint; formerly PIBBSS)
summary: Principles of Intelligence is a nonprofit with a remote team, registered as a US 501(c)(3) in Minnesota. It aims to build scientific foundations for alignment by bringing in researchers and methods from outside mainstream AI safety. It runs the PIBBSS Fellowship, a 3-month programme (London, June to September 2026) that pairs about 20 researchers from fields studying complex and intelligent behaviour with AI-safety mentors. It also coordinates research networks and affiliate groups (Iliad, AFFINE, AIXI Labs, Stormglass, a Fields Institute postdoc), and an internal team works on physics- and maths-inspired interpretability.
why_it_matters: It is the field's main pipeline for turning biologists, physicists, neuroscientists and social scientists into alignment researchers, and the nearest existing model for the widening int/a has in mind. It is also a test case for how far such programmes drift toward mainstream technical agendas.

key_work.title: PIBBSS Fellowship (annual since 2022; 2026 cohort in London, Jun-Sep)
Fields Institute postdoctoral fellowship in mathematical foundations of interpretability
Internal 'Ambitious Mech Interp' research and interpretable architectures
Summer 2026 PIBBSS Fellowship Symposium

The internal research has moved toward mechanistic interpretability and physics- and maths-based theory of deep learning, and most affiliates are formal or agent-foundations groups. The focus on biological and social systems now lives mainly in the fellowship.

Ring: core (E1), because building foundations for alignment is its founding mission and it is funded and staffed from the x-risk ecosystem (SFF, AISI, Coefficient Giving). Transfer: into_model, because its main purpose is scientific understanding of AI systems; 'people' is a second problem because the fellowship widens who does alignment work. Region is global (O: US-registered, fully distributed). London is coded as a hub for the in-person fellowship and London-based staff. Status is changed because of the rename. Framing is catastrophic by its x-risk ecosystem context; the mission statement itself names no stakes.

name: Aintelope
summary: Aintelope is a small AI-safety group that began in 2022 as 'three guys' working in their spare time, and now has a German nonprofit (aintelope gemeinnützige UG) and a UK company. Its agentic strand, built mainly by Roland Pihlakas, makes open-source gridworld benchmarks that test whether RL and LLM agents can handle homeostasis, bounded and multiple objectives, diminishing returns and resource sharing. It also probes when LLMs collapse into unbounded maximisation. A newer consciousness strand, funded by the California Institute for Machine Consciousness, builds agents with attention self-models and presented a position paper at the AAAI 2026 symposium on machine consciousness.
why_it_matters: It makes bounded, homeostatic objectives drawn from physiology and economics a concrete, testable alignment target, in place of open-ended maximisation. It also treats measuring machine consciousness as an empirical problem in multi-agent settings, work that frontier labs rarely fund.

key_work.title: From homeostasis to resource sharing: Biologically and economically aligned multi-objective multi-agent AI safety benchmarks
Black-box interpretability methodology blueprint: Probing runaway optimisation in LLMs
Frontiers in Self Attention and Artificial Consciousness (AAAI 2026 Symposium on Machine Consciousness)
Biological compatibility benchmarks (open-source, MPL 2.0)

funding: Consciousness strand funded by a grant from the California Institute for Machine Consciousness. The agentic work appears to be largely volunteer. No other funders found.

Expression-of-interest form for expected remote-first roles in multi-agent RL, LLM steering and interpretability, philosophy of mind, AI governance and science communication
caveats: Its public footprint is thin: a Google Sites page with few dated updates. The 'three guys in their spare time' description dates from 2022 and no longer fits the eight-person team list. The agentic-benchmark and consciousness strands are fairly separate, and Pihlakas is listed as a collaborator rather than core staff. Neither the arXiv benchmark paper nor the LessWrong posts are peer reviewed.
tag_notes: Home: life (life_neuro), because it describes itself as 'AGI research inspired by neuroscience', follows Byrnes' brain-like AGI paradigm and imports physiological homeostasis into agent objectives; minds is secondary for the CIMC-funded consciousness strand, and economics for the diminishing-returns and bounded-utility concepts. Ring: core (E1), because it was founded as an AI-safety project in the LessWrong and EA ecosystem (VAISU, Foresight, IASEAI). Transfer: into_model, because the benchmarks and attention-schema agents target agent design and behaviour. Assurance is paired with agency because it builds evaluations (F must-pair); ai_status covers the consciousness work. Framing is catastrophic because the work centres on runaway unbounded optimisation and 'the risks of developing AGI-like cognitive architecture' (L: harm-avoiding work takes a harm framing despite the hopeful tagline). Region is europe, by its original German legal base, though the team is spread across Germany, the UK and Estonia.

name: ANU School of Cybernetics
summary: A school of the Australian National University, founded in 2021 by Genevieve Bell, that re-establishes cybernetics as an applied discipline for 'navigating major societal transformations'. It runs a one-year Master of Applied Cybernetics, a cohort-based PhD programme, short courses and the Cybernetic Imagination Residency. Its AI work includes the 'AI Adoption in Australia' survey with Google (2026), 'LLMs Unplugged' AI-literacy workshops for schools, public servants and academics, and art-and-AI projects.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few institutions training practitioners to treat AI as one component of socio-technical systems, using the cybernetics tradition (Beer, Bateson, second-order cybernetics) that mainstream AI safety rarely draws on. That makes it a natural partner for systems-level AI governance and public AI-literacy work.

key_work.title: AI Adoption in Australia (with Google): national survey of 3,500+ adults on generative AI use and governance expectations
LLMs Unplugged / My First LLM: computer-free AI-literacy workshops
Master of Applied Cybernetics (reaccredited for five years in 2025)

Ring adjacent (E3): a sustained AI programme (literacy workshops, adoption survey) framed as 'safe, sustainable and responsible' technology rather than catastrophic risk; one professor's contribution to the International AI Safety Report does not make it a safety programme. Transfer convening (J5): its AI output mainly informs and educates publics, teachers, public servants and students. Framing flourishing is a judgement call from its mission of navigating transformations well.

name: Santa Fe Institute (SFI)
summary: An independent research institute founded in 1984 to study complex adaptive systems across physics, biology, society and technology. Its AI-related work comes from individual faculty: the 'Foundations of Intelligence in Natural and Artificial Systems' workshops (NSF-funded), Melanie Mitchell's research on abstraction and understanding in AI, and a 2025 complexity-science analysis of whether LLM capabilities are 'emergent'. SFI faculty also run sessions for judges on AI, fairness and algorithmic evidence.
why_it_matters: It holds the complexity-science toolkit (emergence, collective computation, multi-scale agency) that AI-safety work on emergent capabilities and multi-agent dynamics mostly lacks. Its sceptical analyses of 'emergence' in LLMs are a corrective to loose capability claims.

key_work.title: Large Language Models and Emergence: A Complex Systems Perspective (Krakauer, Krakauer and Mitchell)
Foundations of Intelligence in Natural and Artificial Systems: A Workshop Report
AI sessions for ~300 judges at the National Judicial Summit, Santa Fe, June 2026 (Moore, Mitchell, Moses)

Ring adjacent (E3): a sustained AI research line (Foundations of Intelligence project, LLM emergence analysis, judges' sessions) with no safety framing. MISFIT: 'adjacent' is defined around societal effects, but SFI's AI work is mostly about understanding AI. name: Centre for Mathematical AI, Fields Institute
summary: A centre at Toronto's Fields Institute for Research in Mathematical Sciences, launched in spring 2025. It works on two questions: how mathematics can make AI systems safer and more transparent, and how AI can help mathematical discovery (formalisation in Lean, AI-assisted reasoning). Its AI-safety strand includes the graduate course 'Mathematics for AI Safety' (autumn 2026) and two-year postdocs, run jointly with PrincInt, on mathematical foundations of interpretability.
why_it_matters: It shows how AI-safety teaching and postdocs can be embedded inside a mainstream mathematics institute. It recruits pure mathematicians and statistical physicists through their own institutions rather than through AI-safety field-building channels.

key_work.title: Mathematics for AI Safety (Fields Academy shared graduate course, MAT1510)
Fields-PrincInt postdoctoral fellowships in mathematics and AI safety
Mathematical AI Seminar 2025-26

Ring bridge (E: an older institution with a new AI-safety programme): the Fields Institute runs a standing AI-safety course and joint PrincInt postdocs. Transfer into_model (J1): the postdoc topics are mathematical foundations of interpretability, though the course also brings mathematicians into AI safety. Framing catastrophic is coded from the course curriculum (capability trajectories, scalable oversight) and the PrincInt partnership; the centre's own wording ('safer and more transparent', 'trustworthiness and alignment') is milder. Status new: the centre launched in spring 2025.

name: Topos Institute (incl. Topos Research UK)
summary: A nonprofit research institute that applies category theory to 'mathematical systems science' and builds open-source modelling software (CatColab, AlgebraicJulia) for collaborative modelling and collective sense-making. It was incorporated in Berkeley in 2019, and its UK sister organisation, Topos Research UK, was incorporated in 2024 and opened an Oxford office that October. Its main AI-safety work is the ARIA Safeguarded AI project 'Double Categorical Systems Theory for Safeguarded AI', which builds a framework for co-designing auditable models of the environments AI systems are deployed in.
why_it_matters: It links formal assurance of AI to collective sense-making: its tools are built to 'enable cooperation across difference', so stakeholders and domain experts can jointly specify what safe AI behaviour means. Its mission language ('knowledge and compassion') is close to int/a's.

name: Glaive Research (Glasgow Lab for AI Verification, GLAIVE)
summary: A small nonprofit research group 'applying category theory to AI verification', using container theory and dependent lenses. It has three programmes: typed tactics for theorem proving in Lean, neural-network architectures built on containers, and Polylang, a programming language whose unit of computation is the lens. It held ARIA Safeguarded AI TA1.1 funding ('True Categorical Programming for Composable Systems') in 2024-25, and its 2025-26 work is an AI-for-maths project on structured tactics for machine-assisted theorem proving.
why_it_matters: It represents the programming-language and category-theory route to verifiable AI, outside both mainstream ML and the AI-safety mainstream. Its tooling aims to make AI theorem provers and network architectures structurally checkable.

key_work.title: True Categorical Programming for Composable Systems (ARIA Safeguarded AI TA1.1)

The ARIA project is closed and Jade Master, its co-lead, is no longer listed on the team. The site gives no founding date or address: 2024 is inferred from the first ARIA awards, and Glasgow from the name ARIA uses. It shares people with the CyberCat Institute (Institute for Categorical Cybernetics), which develops 'theory and software for governing systems that learn and make decisions'.
tag_notes: Home formal (formal_maths): category theory, dependent type theory and programming-language design. Ring bridge (E3): rooted in the applied category theory and PL community, with the mission 'applying category theory to AI verification' and ARIA Safeguarded AI funding in 2024-25. Transfer into_model (J1): typed tactics and container-based architectures change how AI provers and networks are built. MISFIT (framing): GLAIVE states no stakes; 'catastrophic' is inherited from the ARIA Safeguarded AI programme that funded it, and its 2026 work is AI-for-maths tooling.

name: Iliad
summary: A nonprofit founded in 2025 by Alexander Gietelink Oldenziel and Caleb Rak to make foundational AI alignment a 'rigorous scientific field' grounded in mathematics and physics. It runs the four-week Iliad Intensive (from April 2026) and the three-month Iliad Fellowship (with PrincInt), the ILIAD and Agent Foundations conference series, and supports the Alignment Journal. It also incubates four research groups: AIXI Labs, Principia, Stormglass and XOR Labs.
why_it_matters: It is the main training and incubation route that brings mathematicians, theoretical physicists and theoretical computer scientists into alignment research. It imports those disciplines' standards of rigour, giving people from formal fields a concrete way in.

Ring core (E1): founded in 2025 inside the AI-safety ecosystem, funded by Coefficient Giving, and on the aisafety.com map. Transfer into_model (J1): the research it trains and incubates aims at theories of AI systems; 'people' is the second problem because training mathematicians widens who does the work. Region north_america by legal base (its fiscal sponsor is a US 501(c)(3)), with regular London cohorts hosted at LISA.

name: Resolution (incorporating Timaeus)
summary: An alignment research nonprofit launched in June 2026, when Timaeus (founded 2023, known for applying singular learning theory to alignment) joined researchers from UK AISI's Alignment Team. It was briefly announced as Sequent, and legally it is Timaeus Research, Inc. renamed Resolution Alignment, Inc. It pursues a portfolio of theory and empirical bets for 'higher-confidence' alignment of superintelligence: singular learning theory, learning theory, scalable oversight, game theory, persona structure and theory-guided automated research. In September 2026 it added an Agent Foundations team continuing MIRI's line of work.
why_it_matters: It is the best-funded attempt to apply mathematical traditions (singular learning theory, agent foundations, game theory) to alignment at frontier scale, so it will show whether such imported theory can affect how deep learning is done. Its agent-foundations agenda includes work on trust and legitimacy, and it advertises a philosophy research role.

name: Center for Humans and Machines (CHM), Max Planck Institute for Human Development
summary: A research centre at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development in Berlin, set up in 2019 and directed by Iyad Rahwan. It studies how AI and digital media change the way people think, work, cooperate and govern, mainly through behavioural experiments with people and machines (the 'machine behaviour' research line). In 2025 it published two Nature papers: one showing that delegating tasks to AI increases dishonest behaviour, and one proposing a 'science fiction science' method for testing a technology's social effects before it exists. It also hosts the Machine+Behavior conference and an Artist & AI residency.
why_it_matters: It produces experimental evidence on how AI agents change human moral behaviour and cooperation, a question the alignment field mostly handles in theory; the delegation results bear directly on guardrails for agentic AI. It is in Berlin, within reach of int/a's Berlin community.

key_work.title: Delegation to artificial intelligence can increase dishonest behaviour (Nature)
The science fiction science method (Nature)
Machine+Behavior Conference, Harnack Haus, Berlin, 18-19 May 2026

caveats: It frames its work around societal disruption and human moral agency, not AI safety or catastrophic risk. Some strands (social-reward fine-tuning of LLMs, human-AI hybrid systems) sit close to capabilities research. Staff size is an estimate, and individual research groups were not checked.
tag_notes: Home psych (H1: behavioural-experimental method; the taxonomy itself uses CHM as the psych_social example); secondary life for its cultural-evolution and 'machine culture' work, and arts for the science-fiction-science method and the artist residency. Ring adjacent (E3): a sustained AI programme framed around disruption of cognition, morality and cooperation, with no catastrophic-risk, alignment or 'AI going well' framing. Transfer into_institutions (J3): the delegation and guardrail findings are aimed at designers and regulators of agentic AI; social-reward fine-tuning of LLMs is a smaller into_model strand.

name: Jeremy Coller Centre for Animal Sentience, London School of Economics (LSE)
summary: An LSE research centre opened in autumn 2025 with a £4 million multi-year gift from the Jeremy Coller Foundation, directed by the philosopher Jonathan Birch. It studies animal sentience and uses the science to shape policy, law, veterinary practice and public attitudes. One of its four priority areas, Animals and AI, has a dedicated research officer and covers AI in farming, aquaculture and slaughterhouse monitoring. Planned work includes an independent sector report and a code of practice to help the AI industry take animals' interests into account.
why_it_matters: It asks whose interests AI should serve and extends the answer to non-human animals, whom AI-safety value frameworks rarely include. Birch's precautionary framework for 'sentience candidates' is also one of the main methods AI-welfare researchers borrow, though the centre itself does not work on AI sentience.

Ring adjacent (E3): a standing Animals and AI priority area with a dedicated research officer, framed around harms and benefits to animals rather than safety, alignment or AI welfare. Transfer protecting (J4): the centre defends animals, its constituency, from AI deployments. MISFIT: the taxonomy has no problem column for non-human animals affected by AI, so it is coded justice ('whose interests count') plus values (chatbot behaviour, industry code of practice).

name: The Neurorights Foundation (NRF)
summary: A US nonprofit co-founded by the Columbia neuroscientist Rafael Yuste, the human-rights lawyer Jared Genser and Jamie Daves, and run by Executive Director Stephen Damianos. It campaigns for mental privacy, mental identity, free will, fair access to mental augmentation and protection from bias. Its main concern is neurotechnology whose neural data generative AI can increasingly decode. It has backed neural-data laws in Colorado, California and Montana, constitutional changes in Chile and Mexico, and a 2022 UN Human Rights Council resolution. It advised on the US MIND Act (Sept 2025), and in 2024 published a review of consumer neurotech companies' data practices.
why_it_matters: It works on the legal frontier where AI meets direct access to human minds, using a human-rights-law method for cognitive liberty that AI-safety work on manipulation and mental autonomy has barely touched. Its model laws are templates that could extend from neural data to other forms of mind inference.

key_work.title: Safeguarding Brain Data: Assessing the Privacy Practices of Consumer Neurotechnology Companies
Expert consultation on the US MIND Act (Schumer, Cantwell, Markey)
Industry accountability workshop and consumer neurotech scorecard at Asilomar for the Brain and Mind

funding: Not disclosed; its IRS charity profile shows modest programme spending (about $90k on its consumer neurotechnology report).
status_evidence: Mar-Apr 2026: led an industry accountability workshop at Asilomar for the Brain and Mind (about 250 participants); 9 Apr 2026: its legal adviser testified on Vermont neurotechnology bill H.814.
engage: 'Get Involved' page on its website (donations, participation)

caveats: Its subject is neurotechnology governance; AI comes in as the technology that makes neural decoding possible. Per the roster, it does not yet address chatbots' cognitive or emotional effects. The founding year is the IRS ruling year (2022); the founders worked on neurorights earlier through Columbia.
tag_notes: Home law (H1: its method is human-rights law, legislation and advocacy); secondary life because a neuroscientist co-founded and chairs it. Ring adjacent (E3): sustained work on AI-enabled neural decoding and mental privacy, framed as rights, not catastrophic risk or alignment. Transfer into_institutions (J3): it drafts and backs statutes, constitutional amendments and a UN resolution.

name: Amaranth Foundation: NeuroAI for AI Safety
summary: The Amaranth Foundation is a longevity and neuroscience philanthropy that says it has committed over $50M since 2021 to work on brain ageing, centenarian genetics, neurotechnology and NeuroAI. Its NeuroAI team, led by Patrick Mineault, produced 'NeuroAI for AI Safety' (arXiv, Nov 2024; revised Apr 2025) with 15 authors from the foundation, Basis, Convergent Research, E11 Bio, Stanford's Enigma Project, the Allen Institute, Yale and NYU. The roadmap assesses routes from neuroscience to safer AI: brain-like sensory representations, embodied digital twins, biophysical models, cognitive architectures, fine-tuning on brain data, loss functions taken from biology, and neuroscience methods for interpretability.
why_it_matters: It is the main reference document for using neuroscience as a source of AI-safety methods, a route the ML-centred field has largely ignored. A funder from outside the AI-safety ecosystem that has staff on this question is rare.

key_work.title: NeuroAI for AI Safety (roadmap, arXiv 2411.18526)
NeuroAI for AI safety: A Differential Path (LessWrong post)
'Does the solution to building safe artificial intelligence lie in the brain?' (The Transmitter)
'A framework for NeuroAI', talk at Academia Sinica

funding: The foundation reports over $50M donated and committed since 2021 across longevity, neuroscience and NeuroAI (its own figure). No amounts found for grants specific to NeuroAI safety.
status_evidence: 29 Jan 2026: NeuroAI lead Patrick Mineault gave 'A framework for NeuroAI', covering adversarial robustness and AI safety, at Academia Sinica, Taipei.
engage: Newsletter and contact address (neuroaisafety@amaranth.foundation) on neuroaisafety.com
No open grant call for NeuroAI safety found for 2025-26
caveats: No visible grant programme or institutional follow-through on the roadmap in 2025-26 beyond talks and essays. Founders and legal seat are not given on its site: the NeuroAI lead is based in New York, while grant databases list a Philadelphia address. Brain-inspired AI could also speed up capabilities, a tension the roadmap itself raises with its 'differential' framing.
tag_notes: Home life (H4: a one-programme funder goes to that programme's tradition; the taxonomy names Amaranth as Life & systems). Ring bridge (E3): a longevity and neuroscience philanthropy with a standing NeuroAI-for-safety line (staff lead, roadmap, talks into 2026); the taxonomy also uses it as a bridge example. Transfer into_model (J1): the roadmap's routes all target AI systems' representations, training and interpretability. Framing catastrophic is the closest fit for its general 'safe AI' harm framing; the roadmap does not dwell on catastrophe. Scale 'programme in a larger org' because the unit is the NeuroAI line inside a funder.

name: Eon Systems PBC
summary: A San Francisco public-benefit corporation, founded by Michael Andregg, that is building whole-brain emulations from connectomics, expansion microscopy and functional imaging, under the mission 'brain emulation so humans can flourish in a world with superintelligence'. In March 2026 it announced what it called the first embodied emulation of an adult fruit fly brain (about 139,000 neurons and 50 million connections) controlling a simulated body, a claim critics disputed as not yet a true 'upload'. The brain model builds on a 2024 Nature model by its head of engineering, Philip Shiu, and colleagues. Eon raised a $3.5M seed round, led by Protocol Labs, in December 2025.
why_it_matters: It offers brain emulation as an alternative, possibly more legible, path to general intelligence, and pitches it as a way for humans to keep pace with superintelligence. It is a concrete test case for int/a's 'speed of wisdom' question: does emulation help safety, or add another race?

key_work.title: Embodied whole-brain emulation of an adult fruit fly in a simulated body
A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing (Shiu et al., Nature)
$3.5M seed round led by Protocol Labs

funding: $3.5M seed (Dec 2025) led by Protocol Labs, with Untapped Ventures and Larry Page's family office (per Seedtable).
status_evidence: Mar 2026: announced an embodied whole-brain emulation of an adult fruit fly (press coverage 7-11 Mar 2026).
engage: Careers page on eon.systems; about six roles listed on Simplify in 2026
'Partner with Eon' contact on its homepage
caveats: It is contested whether whole-brain emulation helps safety or simply opens another capabilities race. At the time of announcement, the embodied fly result had not been released for independent checking (The Decoder). The neuron model is a simple threshold model, and reported neuron counts vary (125k-139k). Press calls Wissner-Gross a co-founder; the site lists him as founding advisor. The founding year comes from a jobs aggregator. Emulations would also raise digital-minds welfare questions, which Eon does not discuss publicly.
tag_notes: Home life (B4: neuroscience used to build AI; connectomics and computational neuroscience). Ring bridge, the roster value (E): its identity, staff and funding sit in neurotech rather than the AI-safety ecosystem, though its mission is framed around superintelligence and its advisers (Sandberg, Hanson) link it to longtermist circles; arguable as core. Transfer into_model (J1): it builds an alternative, brain-derived form of AI. Power is secondary because it pitches emulation as a democratic alternative to opaque AGI.

name: Brain-inspired Cognitive Intelligence Lab (BrainCog Lab), Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
summary: A lab at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Automation in Beijing, founded in June 2013 and directed by Yi Zeng. It builds brain-inspired AI on spiking neural networks: the BrainCog engine and the BORN engine for what it calls 'living' AGI. A recurring line of its work argues that AI safety and morality should come from brain-like self-models, theory of mind and empathy rather than external constraints. Papers include a 2022 theory-of-mind network for reducing risks to other agents, altruistic and moral agents built on brain-inspired empathy (2024-25), and 'Super Co-alignment' (2025). Zeng also founded the institute's International Research Center for AI Ethics and Governance and is founding dean of the Beijing Institute of AI Safety and Governance.
why_it_matters: It is the clearest non-Western bridge from neuroscience to alignment. It treats alignment as something grown from within, through empathy and self-modelling, rather than imposed, which gives a contrasting alignment target. Zeng links this lab work to Chinese and UN AI governance.
