engage: BrainCog is described as an open platform for brain-inspired AI and brain simulation (braincog.ai); no open calls, jobs or events found in 2025-26
caveats: The lab also pursues 'living AGI' and 'conscious living AI', so its safety work sits beside a capabilities agenda. The lab website's news section has not been updated since 2022, so activity was confirmed through papers. Beijing-AISI, which Zeng founded and leads as dean, is on the classic map, but this lab is not.
tag_notes: Home life (B4: neuroscience and spiking networks used to build AI); secondary philosophy through Zeng's humanities appointment and his human-AI symbiosis ethics. Ring bridge (E3): a brain-inspired AI lab with a standing line of papers (2022-25) explicitly on safety risks, moral AI and superalignment. Transfer into_model (J1): empathy, theory-of-mind and self-model mechanisms are built into agents. The I quadrant reflects its claims about AI self-awareness and empathy as a source of alignment. Standpoint neither (China, per O).

name: Whole Brain Architecture Initiative (WBAI)
summary: A Tokyo-based specified nonprofit, founded in 2015 and chaired by Hiroshi Yamakawa, that promotes building AGI from the architecture of the whole human brain under the motto 'Let's build a brain together'. It maintains Brain Reference Architecture data and tools (BRAES, WholeBIF, CoBRAC), runs hackathons, tutorials, international workshops and a small incentive award, and aims to finish an alpha Whole-Brain Reference Architecture by early 2027. Since its 2026 New Year message it has presented brain-like AGI as a 'bridge' between humanity and superintelligence: a mediator that understands human values from experience and conveys them, while offering an independent reference point for verification.
why_it_matters: It holds a distinctively Japanese thesis: human-like, brain-structured AGI could make AI internals legible and act as a translator of human values to superintelligence. This links to Yamakawa's ALIGN network and its post-singularity symbiosis work.

caveats: It is primarily a brain-inspired AGI effort, which is dual-use, and its safety content is thinner than its AGI content. Its operating budget is very small, so it works largely through volunteers and partner projects. ALIGN, Yamakawa's AI-alignment network, is a separate organisation.
tag_notes: Home life (B4/B5: neuroanatomy-based reference architectures used to build AGI). Ring bridge (E3): a brain-inspired AGI nonprofit rooted in computational neuroscience, whose 2026 policy and message explicitly frame the work around superintelligence, value transmission and independent verification. Transfer into_model (J1): its output is a design specification for AI systems. Framing flourishing because the 2026 message presents a harmonious 'bridge' to superintelligence as the main aim. Standpoint neither (Japan, per O).

name: Partnership for Research Into Sentient Machines (PRISM)
summary: A Cambridge-based charity, launched in March 2025, that builds the field of digital minds: research on AI consciousness and moral status. It runs the 'Exploring Machine Consciousness' podcast and expert workshops, and co-runs a quarterly eight-week Digital Minds online course (cohorts of 100), the Cambridge Digital Minds Fellowship and the Neuromatch AI Sentience Scholarship. It also co-produces the Digital Minds Newsletter and the Beginner's Guide to Digital Minds.
why_it_matters: Most AI-safety field-building ignores whether AI systems themselves might be subjects. PRISM builds talent, public communication and shared resources for that question, and its advisers come from consciousness science (Friston, Solms, Humphrey, Peters, Schneider) rather than ML.

key_work.title: Exploring Machine Consciousness podcast (nine episodes in 2025)

status_evidence: Sep 2026: recruiting a Head of Operations (deadline 30 Sep 2026); PRISM staff co-authored Digital Minds Newsletter #4 (17 Sep 2026).

caveats: Seed-funded by Conscium, a commercial lab working towards conscious or neuromorphic AI, and two of its trustees (Calum Chace, Ed Charvet) are Conscium figures, a possible conflict of interest for a body that sets research principles. The responsible-research principles it promotes were written by Butlin and Conscium's Lappas, and Conscium organised the open letter. The 'world's first' claim at launch is press framing. Its charity number (1184317) dates from around 2019 and its registered objects mention the future of work, so the CIO looks like an existing vehicle repurposed for the March 2025 launch (unverified). Its reported charity income is small next to its visible activity, so the money may run through other channels; this is also unverified.
tag_notes: Home minds/minds_welfare: digital-minds field-building, talent and networks (named as a taxonomy example). Secondary arts for its media method (podcast, public communication). Ring core (E1): founded in 2025 with the primary mission of building the AI-consciousness and moral-status field, and partnered inside the AI-safety ecosystem (Rethink Priorities, FIG, BlueDot, Cambridge Digital Minds). Transfer convening (J5): its main purpose is to communicate, convene and train the digital-minds community; the principles letter is a minor into_institutions strand. Framing MISFIT: no explicit stakes language ('preparing society for the challenges posed by AI consciousness', 'moral seriousness'); coded catastrophic as the closest fit under rule L (mass digital suffering). Status new: launched 17 Mar 2025.

name: Digital Sentience Consortium (Longview Philanthropy with The Navigation Fund and Macroscopic Ventures; 2026 round: Longview Digital Minds RFP)
summary: A pooled funding call, hosted by Longview Philanthropy with The Navigation Fund and Macroscopic Ventures. Its 2025 round (May to July) offered research fellowships, career-transition fellowships and an RFP for applied work on AI consciousness, sentience and moral status. In 2026 Longview ran a second round under its own name, the Digital Minds RFP, which closed on 24 July 2026: project grants of typically $50k–$2M, research fellowships at $55k–$150k a year, and career-development fellowships, with Future Impact Group helping review them.
why_it_matters: It was the first large-scale funding call dedicated to digital minds (per the Digital Minds Newsletter) and remains its main open funding stream. It pays neuroscientists, legal scholars, social scientists and communicators, not only ML researchers, to work on AI welfare measurement, introspection, legal status and governance under uncertainty about moral status. Longview also runs a discretionary Digital Minds Fund for major donors.

key_work.title: Digital sentience funding opportunities: research fellowships, career-transition fellowships and applied-work RFP (deadline 9 Jul 2025)
Request for Proposals: Research and Applied Work on Digital Minds (closed 24 Jul 2026)
Funding of Neuromatch AI Sentience Scholars

status_evidence: Jul 2026: Longview's Digital Minds RFP round closed on 24 Jul 2026 (EA Forum announcement, 6 Jul 2026).

Enquiries: digitalminds-rfp@longview.org

tag_notes: Home minds/minds_welfare under H4: a one-programme funder takes its programme's tradition, here the field's funders. Secondary law and life because it explicitly recruits legal scholars and neuroscientists. Not a generalist funder under rule K. Ring core (E1): dedicated AI-welfare funding from AI-safety-ecosystem funders. Transfer into_model (J1, funders coded by the work they fund): its largest technical lines are welfare measurement, introspection and correlates of consciousness in models; governance, legal and communications tracks are secondary. Problems pair ai_status with minds (rule F), since the call explicitly covers harms from false attribution. Framing flourishing from its aim statement ('ensure that digital minds, if they exist, can both flourish and promote human wellbeing'). Status changed: the consortium closed after 2025 and the 2026 round ran as Longview's own Digital Minds RFP.

name: Digital Minds Newsletter
summary: A quarterly Substack newsletter, launched in December 2025, that collates news, research, debates, funding opportunities and events on AI consciousness, welfare and moral status. Its first issue was a year-in-review mapping the field's organisations. Issues are written by Lucius Caviola, Bradford Saad and Will Millership, joined in 2026 by PRISM staff, and it has over 1,000 subscribers.
why_it_matters: It works as the digital-minds field's shared map and news digest. It links academic consciousness science and philosophy to AI-safety funders, labs' model-welfare work and religious voices such as the Vatican, and it says plainly that it does not advocate.

The Vatican, AI Legal Personhood, and Claude's Constitution (#2)
Functional Emotions and The Pope's Encyclical on AI (#3)
The J-Space Debate, Agent Swarms, and Pacing Frontier AI (#4)

people: Lucius Caviola (co-author; Leverhulme Centre for the Future of Intelligence, Cambridge)
funding: No funding disclosed. PRISM lists it among its own projects.
status_evidence: 17 Sep 2026: published Digital Minds Newsletter #4.
engage: Subscribe free at digitalminds.news (quarterly)
caveats: Young (four issues by Oct 2026) and closely tied to PRISM, whose staff co-write it, so its framing of the field partly reflects one organisation's network.
tag_notes: Home minds under H3: a publication goes with the community it serves, and the taxonomy names this newsletter as its example. Sub minds_welfare as a field network and tracker. Secondary philosophy because a philosopher (Saad) co-writes it. Ring core (E1): its sole purpose is the AI-welfare and digital-minds field, inside the AI-safety ecosystem. Transfer convening (J5): it informs and connects its own field. Framing MISFIT: it calls itself non-advocacy and states no stakes; coded catastrophic as the closest fit under rule L (mass digital suffering is the field's central concern). Org type media. No hub or engagement codes, because newsletters alone do not count.

name: Carboncopies Foundation
summary: A volunteer-heavy US 501(c)(3) founded in 2010 by Randal Koene and Suzanne Gildert to advance whole brain emulation (WBE). It runs the Brain Emulation Challenge, a benchmark that tests brain-reconstruction methods against synthetic ground-truth neural systems, and develops the BrainGenix simulation platform. It also hosts memory-decoding and consciousness journal clubs, gives the Aspirational Neuroscience awards, has drafted an ethics framework for WBE, and offers due-diligence reviews of brain-emulation and brain-interface claims to investors, funders and the press.
why_it_matters: NeuroAI and emulation-based routes to safe AI depend on being able to check whether a reconstructed brain model actually works. Carboncopies holds that ground-truthing and benchmarking know-how and could judge the claims of WBE start-ups. It is a potential partner rather than a safety organisation.

key_work.title: Brain Emulation Challenge and workshop
Workshop: Whole Brain Emulation & AI Safety (with Jaan Tallinn, Anders Sandberg, Ben Goertzel)
Ethics Framework for Whole Brain Emulation
Aspirational Neuroscience Awards at SfN ($25,000 across four memory-decoding papers)

funding: Individual donations to a US 501(c)(3) (EIN 81-4083638); no budget or major donors disclosed.
status_evidence: May 2026: Consciousness & Subjective Experience journal club session; Dec 2025 newsletter.
engage: Volunteer roles (research assistant, complex-systems research, communications, donor relations)
Biweekly Memory Decoding Journal Club and monthly Consciousness & Subjective Experience Journal Club
Workshops and panels, recorded and livestreamed
caveats: Its framing is mind uploading and brain preservation, which comes out of transhumanism; it has not framed its work as AI safety since a single 2019 workshop. The roster's claim that it publishes due-diligence reviews of WBE start-ups such as Eon is not borne out: it offers due diligence as a service and mentions those ventures in its newsletter, but no public review was found. It is incorporated in California, with volunteers on five continents.
tag_notes: Home life/life_neuro: whole brain emulation and connectomics are listed under Neuroscience & NeuroAI. Secondary minds for its consciousness journal club. Ring potential (E2): no AI programme in 2024-26; its one AI-safety event was a 2019 workshop. Transferable method: ground-truth benchmarking of brain-reconstruction methods against synthetic neural systems (Brain Emulation Challenge), plus technical due diligence of emulation claims, both needed by NeuroAI and WBE-based safety proposals. Transfer convening rather than none_yet, because there was some AI-safety convening (the 2019 workshop). Region global and HQ Distributed (rule O): a volunteer-run network with no stated office, incorporated in California.

name: Active Inference Institute
summary: A volunteer-led US 501(c)(3), run online, for research and education on Karl Friston's active inference and free energy principle. It has 2,000+ community members and 700+ livestreams, runs textbook study groups, research fellowships, software projects (e.g. Generalized Notation Notation) and the annual Applied Active Inference Symposium (6th edition 12–13 Nov 2026, online and free). Since June 2025 it has hosted a $270k Survival and Flourishing Fund grant for the AI Capabilities & Alignment Consensus Project, led by Adam Safron.
why_it_matters: Active inference gives a formal, neuroscience-derived account of agency, world models and preferences. The institute is one of the few places where that community works directly on alignment: an SFF-funded project on the meaning of 'world models' and 'agency' that aims to bridge 'doomers' and 'accelerationists', plus fellowship projects on alignment coalitions and on subjectivity in artificial agents.

key_work.title: AI Capabilities & Alignment Consensus Project (AICACP): journal collections, workshops and media; SFF grant of $270k
Research fellowship project 'AI²C: Active Inference Alignment Coalition' (Mahault Albarracin)
6th Applied Active Inference Symposium (12–13 Nov 2026)
The Active Inference Institute & Active Inference Ecosystem (report, v2)

people: Karl Friston (corporate member and scientific adviser)
funding: Survival and Flourishing Fund: $270,000 (2025) for the multi-year AICACP. Crowdfunding (about $20k for Hongju Pae's study of perspective architectures in artificial agents) and donations.
status_evidence: Monthly newsletters through Sep 2026 (latest 30 Sep 2026); 6th Applied Active Inference Symposium scheduled for 12–13 Nov 2026.
engage: 6th Applied Active Inference Symposium, 12–13 Nov 2026 (online, free; presenters and sponsors sought)
Weekly textbook study groups (e.g. Namjoshi, 'Fundamentals of Active Inference')
Volunteer, internship, research-fellowship and mentorship programmes
Livestreams and open repositories
caveats: Volunteer-run, so output quality varies. It is closely networked with VERSES AI (Friston is its chief scientist, and Albarracin works there), which markets 'intrinsically safe' active-inference agents without strong public evidence; claims that active inference solves alignment are unproven. It became an institute in 2022, growing out of the earlier Active Inference Lab. The roster's ring 'potential' was raised to bridge because of the SFF-funded alignment project.
tag_notes: Home life/life_neuro: active inference is listed under Neuroscience & NeuroAI; secondary formal (the mathematics of the free energy principle) and psych (cognitive science). Ring changed from potential to bridge (E3): rooted in theoretical neuroscience, it holds a multi-year SFF-funded project explicitly on AI capabilities and alignment (2025), plus 2026 alignment fellowships, which makes the engagement sustained and explicit. Transfer convening (J5): AICACP's journal collections, workshops and media bring the active-inference community into the alignment debate; fellowship projects on agent design are a smaller into_model strand. Framing MISFIT: consensus-seeking between 'doomers' and 'accelerationists' without taking a side; coded catastrophic because the debate it addresses is about extreme outcomes. Region global (rule O): Delaware-incorporated and fully distributed.

name: Qualia Research Institute (QRI)
summary: A Bay Area 501(c)(3), founded in 2018 by Andrés Gómez Emilsson and Michael Edward Johnson, that seeks a mathematical formalisation of subjective experience and its valence. It combines phenomenological reports from meditative and psychedelic states with psychophysics tools (e.g. the Tracer Replication Tool) and field-based models of consciousness. In November 2025 it sought $1.5M for a 2026 programme of papers, 'consciousness engineering' technologies for pain relief and wellbeing, and an eight-week retreat in Tepoztlán, Mexico.
why_it_matters: Theories of valence and phenomenal binding bear directly on whether, and how, AI systems could suffer. QRI argues that classical digital computers probably cannot have unified experience, a contested but rarely argued view in AI-welfare debates. It has no AI programme, though its 2026 plan names 'working on alignment problems' among its aims without giving details.

key_work.title: Costs of Embodiment (argument that digital computers struggle to produce bound experience)
QRI Research Revealed: From Theory to Consciousness Engineering (2026 fundraiser)
Tepoztlán Retreat 2026 (meditation, research and 5-MeO-DMT studies)

people: Michael Edward Johnson (co-founder; no longer at QRI)
funding: Donations; sought $1.5M for its 2026 research programme (fundraiser presented 20 Nov 2025 in San Francisco). Wikipedia lists Olaf Carlson-Wee (Polychain Capital) on its board.
status_evidence: Dec 2025: published its 2026 fundraiser and research plan; running the Tepoztlán Retreat in 2026.
engage: No AI programme yet (the 2026 plan mentions alignment work in passing): a door to open for researchers or funders who want valence or binding theory applied to AI welfare
Tepoztlán Retreat 2026 (not AI-related)
caveats: Its central theories (Symmetry Theory of Valence, electromagnetic-field accounts of binding) are speculative and largely outside peer-reviewed consciousness science. Its psychedelic research, including 5-MeO-DMT studies at retreat, may concern some funders. Its view that digital computers lack unified experience is a minority position. Its AI engagement is essays and podcasts, mostly by Gómez Emilsson.
tag_notes: Home minds/minds_science (B4): consciousness and valence science, and its AI-relevant output asks whether digital systems can have experience. Secondary contemplative (phenomenology of meditation is a core method) and formal (mathematical and physical models of experience). Ring potential (E2): no standing AI programme; its AI engagement is occasional essays. Transferable method: valence theory and a physical account of phenomenal binding, built from first-person phenomenology and psychophysics, which could test AI-welfare claims. Transfer convening: essays and podcasts bring its view into the AI-welfare conversation; not none_yet, because some AI writing exists. Framing critical for its AI output (deflationary about digital sentience; rule L); its overall mission is suffering-focused and wellbeing-oriented. Badge full_spectrum: first-person phenomenology combined with formal modelling as its method.

name: Neuromatch (incl. AI Sentience Scholars)
summary: A global US 501(c)(3), founded in 2020, that runs online academies in computational neuroscience, deep learning, NeuroAI, computational behaviour and climate science. It reports 13,217 students from 137 countries and a community of 30,000+ including TAs and volunteers. It also runs the Impact Scholars research programme (204 scholars since 2023) and MEXA, a Wellcome-funded community on generative AI for mental health. In 2026 it launched AI Sentience Scholars: a six-month, part-time, Longview-funded programme in which ten early-career researchers apply neuroscience methods to AI sentience. It was developed with PRISM, Cambridge Digital Minds and the Institute of Neuroethics, and its scientific director is Megan Peters.
why_it_matters: It is the largest training pipeline for computational neuroscience and NeuroAI, and AI Sentience Scholars brings empirical consciousness-science methods such as metacognition and psychophysics to AI welfare. Its mentors include Steve Fleming, Axel Cleeremans and Susan Schneider. A NeuroAI-for-safety track would fit the same infrastructure but does not exist yet.

key_work.title: AI Sentience Scholars, 2026 cohort (June–Dec 2026; CIFAR Neuroscience of Consciousness Winter School, Nairobi, 2–5 Dec 2026)
Neuromatch Academy courses in Computational Neuroscience, Deep Learning and NeuroAI
Impact Scholars Program (204 scholars from 31 countries, 48 micropublications)
MEXA: generative AI and mental health community and accelerator (Wellcome-funded)

people: Megan Peters (President and Board Chair; scientific director, AI Sentience Scholars)
Joana Guedes (Science Program Director; leads AI Sentience Scholars and MEXA)
funding: Longview Philanthropy funds AI Sentience Scholars (up to $8k research support per scholar, plus funded travel to the CIFAR winter school); Wellcome funds MEXA. Other funders are not listed on its site.
status_evidence: Jun–Dec 2026: first AI Sentience Scholars cohort under way; CIFAR winter school in Nairobi set for 2–5 Dec 2026.
engage: AI Sentience Scholars: applications for the 2026 cohort closed 28 Apr 2026; watch for the next round and for community webinars
Neuromatch Academy online courses (each summer) and volunteer TA roles
Impact Scholars Program (applications Aug–Sep after the academy)
MEXA community on generative AI and mental health
caveats: Its AI-welfare work began in 2026 and is one small programme within a much larger neuroscience-education organisation. The roster called AI Sentience Scholars 'a rare Global South entry point', but the 2026 cohort came from the UK, France, the US, Portugal, Switzerland and Germany; only the winter school is in Nairobi. The roster's '30,000+ trained' conflates students (about 13,000) with the wider community. The roster's ring 'potential' was raised to bridge.
tag_notes: Home life/life_neuro: computational neuroscience and NeuroAI education is its main output (H1). Secondary minds for the AI Sentience Scholars programme (B4). Ring changed from potential to bridge (E3): rooted in neuroscience, it runs a funded 2026 fellowship explicitly on AI sentience and welfare, merged into this profile. Transfer convening (J5): it brings neuroscientists into the AI-sentience field through training. Problems ai_status, then people (widening who does this work through a global talent pipeline). Framing MISFIT: neutral capacity-building language ('responsibly navigate the scientific and societal implications'); coded flourishing as the closest fit, from its mission of inclusive global science. Region global and HQ Distributed (rule O): a US 501(c)(3) with its CEO in Oxford and remote staff.

name: California Institute for Machine Consciousness (CIMC)
summary: A nonprofit research institute in the San Francisco Bay Area, launched on 30 May 2025, that aims to formulate testable theories of machine consciousness and to build 'a culture and an ethical framework' grounded in them. Its Machine Consciousness Hypothesis, set out in a white paper of January 2026, treats consciousness as self-organised second-order perception that increases coherence, and proposes building and analysing artificial systems to test it. It runs salons and conferences (MC0001 at Lighthaven, Berkeley, May 2026; an AAAI Spring Symposium in Burlingame, 7-9 April 2026; Computational Consciousness at CIC Berlin, 11 September 2026) and Ambhasi, a residency of 10-15 people in Goa, run with Edge City and the Consciousness Foundation.
why_it_matters: It is the most organised attempt to turn machine consciousness into a standalone discipline focused on engineering, which will shape how AI-welfare questions are posed and tested. Moral status of potentially conscious AI is one of its four research tracks. Its stated aim to engineer systems that meet consciousness criteria is itself a governance question the AI-safety field has barely addressed.

key_work.title: Foundational White Paper (Machine Consciousness Hypothesis)
Machine Consciousness 0001 conference, Lighthaven, Berkeley (29-31 May)
AAAI 2026 Spring Symposium on machine consciousness, Burlingame
Computational Consciousness: CIMC X Berlin (with Foresight AI Node)

people: Joscha Bach (founder; vision and direction lead, board director)
Lou de Kerhuelvez (Vice President and Program Director, board director)
Jim Rutt (founding board chair, now chairman emeritus)
funding: Not disclosed. Describes itself as an independent non-profit whose research is open source and which has no revenue model, and invites funders and proposals.
status_evidence: Sep 2026: hosted Computational Consciousness, a one-day conference at CIC Berlin (11 Sep 2026); May 2026: MC0001 conference at Lighthaven, Berkeley.
engage: Jobs: engineer and executive assistant postings on cimc.ai/jobs (2026)
Ambhasi residency: about 15 residents, in Goa within the Edge City India pop-up village, run with Edge City and the Consciousness Foundation
Public conferences and salons (San Francisco salons; MC0001 Berkeley, May 2026; Berlin, Sep 2026)
Its site mentions grants and fellowship programmes run by its programme director, but no open call details were found
caveats: It publishes little safety work, and it partly aims to engineer systems that satisfy consciousness criteria, which many in AI welfare would see as a risk rather than a remedy. Computational functionalism, its starting point, is contested. Funders are not named. The cimc.ai site is a JavaScript app, so details were read from its code and from third-party reports. Jim Rutt chaired the board at launch and is now listed as chairman emeritus.
tag_notes: Home minds under B4: its question is whether machines can have experience, whatever the method. Secondary traditions are life (self-organisation and active inference, with Friston and Levin as regular speakers) and psych (Bach's cognitive architectures). Ring bridge kept: it is rooted in consciousness science and cognitive architecture, and one of four standing tracks covers moral status and rights of potentially conscious AI. It is not core: its mission is consciousness science, not AI going well, and it sits outside the x-risk ecosystem despite using Lighthaven as a venue. Transfer into_model: its criteria are architectural and meant to guide engineering and testing of AI systems. Framing flourishing is the closest fit to its own words ('a culture and an ethical framework'). Way of knowing formal is low confidence: it promises formal specification and simulation, but most output so far is conceptual. A one-off Berlin event does not count as a Berlin hub.

name: Conscium
summary: A London AI company founded in 2024 by Daniel Hulme (also WPP's chief AI officer) with Calum Chace, Ted Lappas, Panos Repoussis and Ed Charvet. Its main product, Verifyax (launched June 2025), tests AI agents in simulated environments populated by non-player characters, before and after deployment. It is also developing neuromorphic architectures based on looped language models (Neuroax). A smaller research strand, Frontier, works on machine consciousness under Mark Solms: in February 2025 it organised the Butlin-Lappas 'Principles for Responsible AI Consciousness Research' and an open letter supporting them, and it seed-funded the nonprofit PRISM.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few companies that links agent assurance to consciousness science; its advisory board includes Karl Friston, Mark Solms, Anil Seth and Megan Peters. Its principles are a rare industry statement on when building conscious AI could be justified, and on avoiding the creation of AI systems that suffer.

key_work.title: Principles for Responsible AI Consciousness Research (Butlin and Lappas) and open letter
Verifyax AI agent verification platform launch
Seed funding of PRISM, a nonprofit researching sentient AI
Perspectives on Machine Consciousness (book, ed. Calum Chace and Ted Lappas, CRC Press)

funding: Part-funded by WPP (Guardian, Feb 2025). WPP is also its main partner and first large customer for agent verification. Other investment is undisclosed.
status_evidence: Mar 2026: partnership with UK IT services firm Exponential-e on AI agent assurance for public and private sectors.
caveats: Its revenue comes mainly from agent verification, near the compliance end of this map's scope, and the consciousness research looks secondary. It is closely tied to WPP through its founder and funding. PRISM, which it seed-funded, is a separate organisation.
tag_notes: Home minds: what it imports from outside ML is consciousness science (Solms-led research, an advisory board of neuroscientists, the responsible-research principles, seed money for PRISM), so minds_welfare. Verifyax is ML testing, not a sector under H2; its certification and assurance concepts are drawn on as secondary safety, and the neuromorphic work as secondary life. Ring bridge kept from the roster: it is not core because it sits outside the AI-safety/x-risk ecosystem. MISFIT: a commercial AI company rather than an institution rooted in another field. Transfer into_model: its main product tests the AI agents themselves. Framing present_harms is low confidence; its mission is safe, reliable enterprise deployment ('in AI we cannot safely deploy what we do not understand'), while the consciousness letter alone would read as catastrophic.

name: Association for Mathematical Consciousness Science (AMCS)
summary: A membership association of scientists and philosophers working on mathematical and formal theories of consciousness. It is registered as a German charitable Verein seated in Munich, with its postal address at the University of Bamberg. It runs the annual Models of Consciousness conferences: MoC6 at Hokkaido University (30 Sept-4 Oct 2025) and MoC7 at the University of Copenhagen (12-16 Oct 2026). MoC7 has 'AI, LLMs and consciousness science' as one of four themes and plans a collective consensus paper. In April 2023 AMCS published an open letter, signed by 150+ people including Yoshua Bengio and Manuel Blum, calling for faster consciousness research as part of responsible AI development, and it made a submission to the UN's High-Level Advisory Body on AI.
why_it_matters: It is the professional home of the formal consciousness-theory community, whose measures and models any credible test for AI consciousness would rely on. Its open letter and the AI theme at MoC7 show it starting to turn that community towards AI welfare and safety.

key_work.title: Open letter: The Responsible Development of AI Agenda Needs to Include Consciousness Research
Submission to the UN High-Level Advisory Body on AI on consciousness and AI governance
Models of Consciousness 6, Hokkaido University
Models of Consciousness 7, University of Copenhagen (with AI/LLM theme and consensus paper)

people: Johannes Kleiner (founding board chair, board member)
funding: Membership and donations. MoC7 is supported by a Carlsberg Foundation grant and host universities (Copenhagen, Hokkaido, ShanghaiTech, Bamberg, Oxford, Wisconsin-Madison). No budget published.
status_evidence: Oct 2026: MoC7 at the University of Copenhagen (12-16 Oct 2026), co-organised with the Centre for Philosophy of AI; registration closed 31 Aug 2026.
engage: Models of Consciousness conference, annual (MoC7 Copenhagen, 12-16 Oct 2026)
Membership and mailing list via amcs-community.org/join
Recorded conference talks and seminars online
caveats: Its explicit AI outputs (open letter, UN submission) date from 2023; its current AI engagement is mainly the AI/LLM theme at MoC7, so bridge is borderline. Mathematical consciousness science holds rival theories (integrated information, global workspace and others) and no consensus on whether any applies to AI. Its online seminar series last ran in 2024. Founding year is taken from its constitution (8 Jan 2021); the conference series began in 2019.
tag_notes: Home minds, sub minds_science: it develops theories and measures of consciousness and asks whether they apply to AI (B4, B13). Formal is secondary for its mathematical methods. Ring bridge kept: it is rooted in consciousness science, and its AI programme is framed explicitly around AI safety and moral status through repeated convening (an AI theme at MoC7) and a 2023 letter and UN submission. Borderline under E(2), since most explicit AI outputs predate 2024. Transfer convening: its main act is bringing its own research community into the AI question at its conferences. Org type membership (I): a learned society with elected board and members. Framing catastrophic is low confidence: the letter invokes AI safety, alignment and control, and moral status, without naming catastrophe; no option fits well. The online seminars paused after 2024, so no online hub.

name: Sentient Futures (formerly AI for Animals)
summary: A San Francisco 501(c)(3) founded by Constance Li in 2023 that works to 'make the future go well for all sentient beings, with a particular focus on transformative AI and nonhumans', meaning animals and potentially sentient AI. It runs Sentient Futures Summits: Bay Area, 6-8 Feb 2026, about 250 attendees including staff of frontier labs; London, 22-24 May 2026; next Bay Area, 12-14 March 2027. It also runs an AIxAnimals course, a remote 10-week Project Incubator with 80+ mentors, an in-person residency in San Francisco (first cohort summer 2026), a monthly newsletter and a Slack community of 1,700+ members.
why_it_matters: It is the main meeting point between the animal-welfare movement and AI safety, and pushes nonhuman interests into alignment targets and the digital-minds debate. Incubator projects include benchmarks and training data for how LLMs treat animals, and work on detecting morally relevant properties in AI systems.

key_work.title: Sentient Futures Summit Bay Area 2026 (6-8 Feb, Mox, San Francisco)
AI, Animals & Digital Minds NYC 2025 (conference retrospective)
Project Incubator (remote, 31 Aug-9 Nov 2026), incl. animal-welfare benchmarks for LLMs
SF Residency, first cohort

funding: Coefficient Giving, The Navigation Fund, EA Animal Welfare Fund, Survival and Flourishing Fund, Longview Philanthropy, craigslist Charitable Fund and individual donors, per its site (2026). Amounts not published.
status_evidence: Aug 2026: announced Sentient Futures Summit Bay Area 2027 (12-14 Mar 2027); Project Incubator cohort running 31 Aug-9 Nov 2026.
engage: Sentient Futures Summit Bay Area, 12-14 Mar 2027 (speaker applications due 16 Oct 2026); London summit held each May before EA Global London
Project Incubator: 10-week remote fellowship with a mentor, 5+ hours a week (Aug-Nov 2026 cohort)
SF Residency: 10-15 weeks in San Francisco, expenses covered, rolling applications
AIxAnimals course

caveats: Part of its work is using AI to help animals now, an 'AI for good' strand outside this map's scope; the strand tagged here is making AI go well for nonhumans. Some animal advocates opposed its move into AI welfare (MIT Technology Review, Mar 2026). It is embedded in EA funding networks. It was formerly AI for Animals; that name was still used for its early-2025 Bay Area conference, so the rename appears to date from 2025.
tag_notes: Home minds, sub minds_welfare: the taxonomy places animal sentience bridged to AI and digital-minds field-building and networks here. MISFIT: animal-welfare advocacy, its real root, has no tradition of its own in the taxonomy. Ring bridge kept from the roster: its identity, people and part of its funding come from the animal-welfare movement, and it runs a sustained programme on making transformative AI go well for nonhumans. Core is arguable, since it was founded in 2023 for this purpose with EA funding. Problems: values first, because its distinctive line is how AI values animals (benchmarks, alignment to animal welfare), with ai_status second. Transfer convening: its main purpose is to bring the animal-advocacy community and AI people together to build the field. Framing flourishing follows its own words ('make the future go well for all sentient beings'), low confidence. Status changed: renamed from AI for Animals, same mission (rule: a name change is still changed). The online hub is earned by the remote incubator, course and Slack; London summits are annual, so not a London hub.

name: Sentience Institute
summary: A US social-science think tank founded in June 2017 by Jacy Reese Anthis and Kelly Anthis to study moral circle expansion; since 2023 it has worked mainly on digital minds. Its main instrument is the Artificial Intelligence, Morality, and Sentience (AIMS) survey of US public attitudes to AI sentience and moral status, with waves in 2021, 2023 and 2024 (the last reported in Feb 2026) and a 2023 supplement on AI safety. Its 2025-26 papers cover public risk perception and support for regulating digital minds, perceptions of mind across types of AI, AI companionship, and how mental models of AI autonomy and sentience shape reactions to AI.
why_it_matters: It produces the main long-running data on how the public attributes minds and moral status to AI. That evidence matters for governing digital minds and for anticipating social conflict and attachment as AI seems more sentient. It brings social and moral psychology to a debate otherwise led by philosophers and ML researchers.

key_work.title: AIMS survey, 2024 wave report (open data)
Perceptions of Sentient AI and Other Digital Minds: Evidence from the AIMS Survey
Public Opinion and the Rise of Digital Minds: Perceived Risk, Trust, and Regulation Support
Digital Companionship: Overlapping Uses of AI Companions and AI Assistants

people: Kelly Anthis (co-founder; executive director for its first three years)
funding: Donor-funded 501(c)(3). Received $50,000 from the Survival and Flourishing Fund (Jan 2022) and $80,000 from EA Funds (by mid-2022). No recent budget published; its 2025 end-of-year summary appeals for donations.
status_evidence: Apr 2026: published two papers, on AI companionship and on mental models of AI autonomy and sentience; Feb 2026: AIMS 2024 wave report.
caveats: A small team works largely remotely. Output is a few papers a year, and its 2025 summary asks for donations to keep the work going. AIMS samples are US-only. Its older work on animal farming and social movements continues alongside the digital-minds focus (an Animals, Food, and Technology survey).
tag_notes: Home minds, sub minds_welfare: the taxonomy places public attitudes to AI moral status here, and the institute is led by welfare-focused researchers (B3). Psych is secondary for its social- and moral-psychology survey methods. Ring bridge kept: it is an older moral-circle think tank from animal advocacy that redirected to digital minds in 2023 (E: an old institution with a new AI-welfare programme). Problems pair minds with ai_status (F), because its 2026 work spans attribution and companionship as well as moral status. Transfer into_institutions is low confidence (convening is the alternative): its survey evidence feeds digital-minds governance and advocacy strategy. Framing catastrophic: its research agenda ties digital minds to catastrophic risk and suffering at scale (L: mass digital suffering). Engagement left empty: its site offers only a newsletter and donations.

name: WhenAISeemsConscious.org
summary: A public guide for people who feel that an AI they talk to is conscious, written in June 2025 and launched in August 2025. Its twelve authors are consciousness and AI-welfare researchers, led by Lucius Caviola (Cambridge) with Jeff Sebo, Robert Long, Patrick Butlin, Nick Bostrom, Bradford Saad, Derek Shiller and others. It says current AIs are probably not conscious but this cannot be ruled out. It advises pausing before drawing conclusions, stepping away when distressed, asking the AI technical questions about how it works, avoiding cruelty under uncertainty and not acting drastically on such beliefs. It was last updated in February 2026 and invites readers to share their experiences through a form.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few resources from the AI-welfare side that addresses people's beliefs about, and attachment to, AI they think is conscious. It protects the people involved while treating the AI's own status as an open question, rather than dismissing either concern.

key_work.title: When AI Seems Conscious: public guide
Launch post: A guide about (seemingly) conscious AI (Lucius Caviola)
Updated edition of the guide

people: Lucius Caviola (lead author and contact, University of Cambridge)
Jeff Sebo (co-author, NYU Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy)
funding: No funder or host named.
status_evidence: Feb 2026: guide updated (first written June 2025, launched Aug 2025).
engage: Share an experience with a seemingly conscious AI through the guide's feedback form
caveats: It is a single web guide written by twelve volunteer authors, not an organisation with staff, and it names no host or funder. Its authors come mostly from the AI-welfare community, which takes AI consciousness more seriously than many clinicians or sceptics do; it is not clinical guidance.
tag_notes: Home minds per B3, which names this guide: it addresses mind attribution and is led by consciousness and welfare researchers, not clinicians. Psych is secondary because Caviola works in moral psychology. Sub minds_welfare covers public readiness on AI moral status. Ring changed from bridge to core under E(1): the project exists to handle an AI-transition problem (seemingly conscious AI), and its authors belong to the AI-welfare and x-risk ecosystem (Eleos, Macrostrategy Research Initiative, NYU CMEP, Rethink Priorities). It imports consciousness science and moral psychology. Problems pair minds with ai_status (F), since it covers both human attribution and AI welfare. Transfer protecting: it exists to protect people unsettled by AI, and the authors made it after receiving many emails from such people. MISFIT on org_type: a volunteer project with no host, filed as programme.

name: The Co-Sentience Initiative (CoSI)
summary: A small initiative launched in 2025 to help prepare for a possible future shared with artificial minds. It is funded by an unnamed consortium of philanthropists on three continents. Its main output is CF Debate, a website that maps 13 arguments for and 31 against computational functionalism (the view that the right computation is enough for consciousness), with responses to each, a quiz and FAQs. It pays up to US$100 for substantial corrections or additions. The project lead is Chris Percy, supported by a small team in analytical philosophy, computer science and meta-ethics.
why_it_matters: It turns the central question for AI welfare, whether computation alone can give rise to consciousness, into an argument map that non-specialists and funders can inspect. It brings argument mapping, a collective-epistemics method, into a field that otherwise argues in papers and podcasts.

key_work.title: CF Debate: a structured assembly of arguments for and against computational functionalism

funding: An unnamed consortium of philanthropists across three continents, per its site.
status_evidence: 2025: CF Debate launched (listed in the Digital Minds 2025 year in review); the site's sitemap records a rebuild on 13 Aug 2026.
engage: Paid feedback: substantial corrections or additions to the argument map can earn up to US$100
caveats: Little is public about its team, legal form, base or funders beyond the project lead. Evidence of 2026 activity is limited to a site rebuild. The map lists far more arguments against computational functionalism than for it (31 against, 13 for), which some readers may take as a lean. It says it has other projects under way, but none is public.
tag_notes: Home minds per B13: its subject is the philosophy of mind applied to AI consciousness, so minds_science. Democracy is secondary for the argument-mapping method (B10) and philosophy for its analytic staff. Ring bridge kept from the roster: AI welfare is its founding aim, but its membership of the AI-safety ecosystem cannot be verified, so it is not moved to core. Transfer convening: it informs and gathers the consciousness and AI-welfare community around a shared map, rather than changing models or institutions. Framing flourishing follows its stated aim of 'a positive outcome for all sentient beings', though it also calls the situation high-stakes. Org type nonprofit is unconfirmed (legal form unknown). Region global and hq left empty because no base is stated.

name: Mind & Life Institute (with Mind & Life Europe)
summary: A US nonprofit founded in 1987 by the Dalai Lama, neuroscientist Francisco Varela and lawyer Adam Engle. It built the field of contemplative science through dialogues with the Dalai Lama, research grants and an annual Summer Research Institute. Its three-year strategy (announced June 2025) names 'AI & Technology' as one of four priority areas, and its 39th Dialogue, 'Minds, Artificial Intelligence, and Ethics' (Dharamsala, 14–16 October 2025, co-hosted with Mind & Life Europe), brought about 100 scientists, monastics, philosophers, technologists and policymakers together on intelligence, human–AI relationships, AI narratives, embedding ethics in AI, and education. Its Swiss sister organisation, Mind & Life Europe (Winterthur), runs the biennial European Summer Research Institute, the journal Hyphae and the Enactive Fold podcast, which has run an episode on 'enactive AI' with Luc Steels and Takashi Ikegami.
why_it_matters: It holds the densest network linking contemplative practitioners, including senior Tibetan Buddhist teachers, with neuroscientists and enactive cognitive scientists, and it has put AI on its strategic agenda. That makes it a ready convenor and grant-maker for a contemplative line of work on what intelligence and wisdom mean for AI, which the mainstream safety field does not have.

key_work.title: Mind & Life Dialogue XXXIX: Minds, Artificial Intelligence, and Ethics (Dharamsala)
Three-year strategy naming AI & Technology a priority area
Exploring intelligence, ethics and AI (reflection on Dialogue XXXIX)

funding: 2024 revenue about $3.46M (ProPublica, Form 990). The Dialogue XXXIX page lists the Dalai Lama Trust, the Hershey Family Foundation and the Adam J. Weissman Foundation as supporters, with the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives and the Norbulingka Institute as partners; Mind & Life Europe's share was reportedly supported by the Italian Buddhist Union. By 2020 it had awarded more than $5.2M to over 270 research projects.
status_evidence: Jun 2026: Summer Research Institute on depolarisation at the Garrison Institute; Jan 2026: Sona Dimidjian took over as board chair; Oct 2025: Dialogue XXXIX on AI.
engage: Varela Research Grants for contemplative research (Mind & Life Institute)
Summer Research Institute, held every year by application (2026: 7–12 June, Garrison Institute, NY; applications closed). The site lists AI as a possible future theme
Mind & Life Europe: European Summer Research Institute (biennial; next in 2027, theme 'Opening') and European Varela Awards
Dialogue XXXIX session recordings, free on mindandlife.org
caveats: So far the AI work is one flagship dialogue plus a stated strategic priority. I found no AI grant line or standing AI programme in 2026, and the 2026 Summer Research Institute was on depolarisation. It frames the stakes as human flourishing and societal risks (health, education, work, politics, climate), not alignment or catastrophic risk. Mind & Life Europe is a separate Swiss nonprofit. The institute gives 1987 as its founding year (the first dialogue); Wikipedia gives 1991, probably the year it was incorporated.
tag_notes: Home: contemplative. The taxonomy names Mind & Life as its example of contemplative science (B1: contemplative science, not speaking for a faith); life is secondary for its neuroscience and enactive cognition, religion for the Dalai Lama's and monastics' formal part. Ring: adjacent, kept from the roster (E3). It has a standing 'AI & Technology' strategic priority plus a flagship dialogue, framed around human flourishing and societal risks rather than alignment or catastrophe; it is borderline potential, since the only concrete AI output is one dialogue. Transfer: convening (J5); the dialogue brought its contemplative-science community into the AI conversation. Merged Mind & Life Europe into this profile.

name: Flourishing AI Initiative and Benchmarks (FAI), Gloo
summary: Gloo, a Nasdaq-listed technology company in Boulder, Colorado that serves churches and faith-based nonprofits, runs the Flourishing AI initiative. Its standards (February 2025) and benchmarks score LLMs on seven dimensions of flourishing taken from Harvard's Human Flourishing Program and the Global Flourishing Study: character, relationships, happiness, meaning, health, finances and faith. The general benchmark (FAI, later FAI-G; 1,229 questions; July 2025) found no model acceptably aligned across all seven dimensions. A Christian-worldview version (FAI-C; 807 questions scored by Christian expert judge personas) followed in December 2025, and the June 2026 insights report tested 36 models on both.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few running evaluations that score models against an explicit, multi-dimensional account of human flourishing, including meaning and faith, rather than harm avoidance alone. It is a working template for wisdom or flourishing evals built from social-science constructs, and also a cautionary example of how a sponsor's worldview shapes what counts as 'aligned'.

key_work.title: Measuring AI Alignment with Human Flourishing (FAI Benchmark paper)
Flourishing AI Christian (FAI-C) Benchmark
FAI Insights Report (FAI-G and FAI-C, 36 models)

people: Pat Gelsinger (Executive Chair and Head of Technology, Gloo)
funding: Funded by Gloo Holdings (Nasdaq: GLOO), which raised $22.75M gross in a July 2026 public offering. The benchmark was built with Barna Group and Valkyrie Intelligence.
status_evidence: Jun 2026: second FAI Insights Report, scoring 36 models on FAI-G and FAI-C.
engage: In December 2025 Gloo invited researchers in psychology, philosophy, theology, ethics and AI safety to engage with the evolving benchmark
Insights reports and a leaderboard are published at gloo.com/fai
caveats: The sponsor has a commercial stake. Gloo sells 'values-aligned' AI to faith organisations and reports that its own Christian-worldview fine-tunes score 30+ points higher on the Faith dimension. Scoring relies on judge LLMs with expert personas, and the Faith dimension is defined as communion with God or the transcendent, a contested choice. Harvard's Human Flourishing Program supplied the framework, and Tyler VanderWeele endorsed the standards, but Harvard is not the benchmark's author. The FAI-C methodology paper was promised for peer review in early 2026; I could not confirm it has appeared.
tag_notes: Home: religion, not the provisional psych. The taxonomy places faith benchmarks under Religion, and the 2025–26 outputs centre on the Christian-worldview FAI-C (A2). Psych is secondary because the seven dimensions come from Harvard's flourishing science; under B2, FAI-G alone would be psych_social, so this is a seam entry. Ring: changed from adjacent to bridge (E3). It is rooted in faith tech and runs a sustained programme (standards Feb 2025, benchmark Jul 2025, FAI-C Dec 2025, reports Dec 2025 and Jun 2026) explicitly framed as 'AI alignment with human flourishing'. Transfer: into_model (J1); these are evaluations of model behaviour, also used to tune Gloo's own models. Must-pair under F: values + assurance. org_type: programme (A1, a unit inside a company).

name: Center for Buddhist AI Ethics, CamTech University
summary: A centre at the Cambodia University of Technology and Science (CamTech) in Phnom Penh, launched in June 2023 and directed by Prof. Chhem Kieth Rethy. Its stated vision is AI development guided by Buddhist ethics for human well-being, through research, 'mindful education', policy advocacy and international engagement. It has run a Buddhist AI Ethics seminar series (November 2023, co-organised with Kol Tor Teung Pagoda; August 2024; October 2024, 'Buddhism and AI: Reality, Ethics, and Governance'). In August 2025 it published the edited volume 'Buddhist Mind for AI Machines', with essays on Buddhist ontology, epistemology (catuskoti, sunyata) and ethics (compassionate AI, cetana) applied to AI design.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few institutional nodes working on Buddhist ethics and AI from a Theravada-majority, Southeast Asian country, and its director has a seat in Cambodian government. That gives a route for Buddhist ethical concepts into regional AI discussion, a perspective almost absent from the mainstream field.

key_work.title: Buddhist Mind for AI Machines (edited volume, CamTech University Press)
Buddhist AI Ethics Seminar Series 3: Buddhism and AI: Reality, Ethics, and Governance
'Embracing compassionate AI' seminar and launch of the centre

people: Chhem Kieth Rethy (Director; Distinguished Professor of AI and Humanities; Senior Minister, Cambodia)
Cheab Sambath (co-editor and co-author, Buddhist Mind for AI Machines)
Chhem Siriwat (co-editor; Vice President, CamTech AI Forum)
status_evidence: Aug 2025: published 'Buddhist Mind for AI Machines' (CamTech University Press); the last dated seminar was in Oct 2024.
caveats: I found no 2026 activity; the centre's own page lists events only from 2023–24. The roster's claim of four seminar iterations up to September 2025 could not be confirmed: three numbered Buddhist AI Ethics seminars appear, plus a June 2023 launch seminar that was part of CamTech's general AI Forum series. Its stated concerns are bias, privacy and jobs rather than catastrophic risk. The director is a serving Senior Minister and chairs Cambodia's Economic, Social and Cultural Council. The 2025 book carries an AI-use disclosure and a prompt log. Staff and funding are not disclosed.
tag_notes: Home: religion (B1). It is a Buddhist ethics centre interpreting Theravada, Mahayana and Vajrayana teachings for AI, and has co-organised seminars with a pagoda; rel_buddhist lists ethics centres. Philosophy is secondary for the director's philosophy-of-technology work. Ring: adjacent, kept. It is a standing centre with a seminar series (2023–24) and a 2025 book, focused on Buddhist ethics and present concerns rather than alignment or catastrophic risk, though its 2023 launch used some 'alignment with human values' language. Transfer: convening (J5). Its seminars and book address Cambodian academic and Buddhist audiences; I found no evidence that its design proposals have reached models or policy instruments. Standpoint: majority_world, as it is led from Cambodia.

name: Wisdom Beyond
summary: A small, self-described women-led collective in Northern California that runs multi-day, application-only retreats for technologists and leaders on AI and contemplative, somatic practice. Its sixth cohort, 'Beacons of Resonance: A retreat on AI & Attunement' (15–19 October 2026, Teravana forest retreat, Cazadero), proposes moving 'beyond alignment as control, toward attunement as relationship'. Earlier cohorts were themed AI & Alignment, AI & Regeneration, AI & Collective Intelligence, AI & Interbeing, and AI & Consciousness. The site says this is likely one of its last public retreats; later gatherings will be private and invite-only.
why_it_matters: It offers embodied, somatic and contemplative formation aimed specifically at the people building AI, and treats the relationship between people and AI ('attunement') as the design question. This inner-work angle is largely missing from mainstream safety programmes.

key_work.title: Beacons of Resonance: A retreat on AI & Attunement (sixth cohort)

people: Raiya Kind (facilitator; described as Head of AI/ML Research Collaboration at Google X)
Raina DeLear (facilitator; co-founder, Luminous Body Integral School of Energy Medicine)
Kristen Greco (facilitator; somatics practitioner, Luminous Awareness Institute)
funding: Participant applications and sponsors (the site links a sponsorship deck); amounts not disclosed.
status_evidence: Oct 2026: sixth cohort retreat (15–19 Oct), applications extended to 5 Oct 2026.
engage: Apply for the October 2026 'Beacons of Resonance' retreat (deadline 5 October 2026, 5pm PT); later gatherings will be invite-only
Sponsorship and partnership deck linked from the homepage
caveats: All information is self-published: I found no independent coverage, and alumni and testimonials are anonymous. The roster said facilitators are unnamed, but the site's facilitators page names three; two come from energy medicine. The founding year and legal form are not stated. It is moving to private, invite-only gatherings.
tag_notes: Home: contemplative, cont_practice (B1, B2). It runs retreats in somatic, energy-medicine and contemplative practice for AI builders and leaders. Ring: changed from adjacent to bridge (E3). It has run six AI-themed cohorts (including 'AI & Alignment'), explicitly framed around the AI paradigm and 'attunement' as an alternative to alignment-as-control, so this is not only about AI's human effects. Transfer: into_builders (J2); the retreats change participants as people. MISFIT: the legal form is not stated and it calls itself a 'women-led collective', so I coded it network. I considered the inner_outer badge but did not give it, because evidence of outer change is self-reported.

name: Glorisun Global Network for Buddhist Studies
summary: An academic network for Buddhist studies, launched in January 2017 and funded by the Glorisun Charitable Foundation of Hong Kong industrialist Charles Yeung. It links 14 institutions, among them Peking University, UBC, Oxford, Cambridge, Harvard, Princeton, Yale, Berkeley, Hamburg, Tokyo and Inalco, and runs conferences, summer programmes, fellowships, visiting-scholar schemes and the Hualin publications. Its only AI-related activity found is the 'Buddhism and Global Governance' symposium at Inalco, Paris (9–10 July 2025), on AI, regional conflicts and climate change, with sessions on Buddhist ethics and AI ethics; Chinese and English collections were planned.
why_it_matters: It is a well-funded bridge between Chinese and Western Buddhist scholarship that has begun, lightly, to ask what Buddhist ethics offers AI governance. That could open a rare channel to Chinese Buddhist scholars and philanthropy on AI.

key_work.title: International Symposium on Buddhism and Global Governance (AI, regional conflicts and climate change), Inalco, Paris

people: Charles Yeung (Principal Advisor; founder of the Glorisun Charitable Foundation)
Jinhua Chen (Associate Board Director, University of British Columbia)
funding: Glorisun Charitable Foundation (established 2005 by Charles Yeung). The 2025 symposium was also sponsored by the China-Britain Trust for the Promotion of Buddhist Studies.
status_evidence: Jul 2026: conferences in Hangzhou and Shaoxing and an intensive summer programme with Peking University (no AI content); Jul 2025: Paris symposium with an AI strand.
engage: Fellowships, postdoctoral support and visiting-scholar and visiting-student schemes in Buddhist studies (not AI-specific)
No AI programme: outreach needed to develop the 2025 symposium's AI-ethics strand
caveats: AI was one strand of a single symposium. The network's own conference page still lists the 2025 Paris events as upcoming, with no report or proceedings, so I could not confirm the planned collections appeared. The 2026 programme has no AI content. It is a philology and history network rather than an ethics or AI body, so it was still a one-off at the time of writing.
tag_notes: Home: religion (B1). It is a Buddhist-studies network funded by a Buddhist charitable foundation, and rel_buddhist covers Buddhist scholarship networks and funders. Ring: changed from adjacent to potential (E2); AI was one strand of a single symposium (Paris, Jul 2025), and the 2026 programme has no AI content. Transferable method: a funded network linking Chinese and Western Buddhist-studies scholars that could host sustained work on Buddhist ethics (compassion, non-violence) for AI governance. Transfer: convening (J5), not none_yet, because of the 2025 symposium. The systemic problem tag reflects that the symposium placed AI alongside conflict and climate under global governance; the evidence is thin. Region: global, since it is coordinated jointly from Peking University and UBC with no single base.

name: John Vervaeke's Lectern and Vervaeke Foundation ('Mentoring the Machines')
summary: The education platform of University of Toronto cognitive scientist John Vervaeke: the video series Awakening from the Meaning Crisis, After Socrates and Voices with Vervaeke, plus The Lectern, a paid platform of live and self-study courses and a membership community. Its AI output is 'Mentoring the Machines' (Story Grid Publishing, one book in four parts released December 2023 to April 2024), co-written with editor Shawn Coyne. The book treats alignment as cultivating wisdom in AI and in the people who build it, and asks ordinary people ('the Commons'), not tech elites or governments, to take part. The Vervaeke Foundation's domain now redirects to his personal site.
why_it_matters: Vervaeke's cognitive science of relevance realisation and wisdom cultivation, and his meaning-crisis framing, are central to the metamodern milieu int/a draws on. He offers a theory of wisdom that could inform alignment targets, and an account of how AI deepens the meaning crisis.

key_work.title: Mentoring the Machines (with Shawn Coyne, four parts)
Awakening from the Meaning Crisis (lecture series)

people: John Vervaeke (founder; Professor, Psychology and Cognitive Science, University of Toronto)
Shawn Coyne (co-author, Mentoring the Machines; founder, Story Grid)
funding: Lectern subscriptions and course fees, and Patreon. No foundation filings found.
status_evidence: May 2025: 'What AI Can Never Be' (on whether AI can be wise) and 'Hacking Humanity' (algorithmic manipulation) episodes on his podcast feed; 2025 episodes with Mastropietro and Jordan Hall on 'intimate AI' and with Sam Tideman on 'AI sages'; Sep 2026: The Lectern offering 2026 courses. Mentoring the Machines was completed in April 2024.
engage: The Lectern: live weekly courses, self-study courses and the Lectern Lounge membership community (not AI-specific)
Patreon and YouTube series
No AI programme: outreach needed to bring relevance-realisation work to alignment research
caveats: This is essentially an individual-led platform rather than an organisation; the map's unit is the organisation, so it is a borderline inclusion. vervaekefoundation.org now 301-redirects to johnvervaeke.com, and I could not establish whether the foundation still operates. AI is a recurring topic in his 2024–25 podcast output, but there is no funded AI research programme, and Mentoring the Machines is a popular book.
tag_notes: Home: contemplative, cont_integral (B7). The taxonomy places the metamodern milieu in Contemplative, and Vervaeke's meaning-crisis and wisdom-cultivation work sits at its centre; psych (cognitive science of relevance realisation) and philosophy are secondary. Ring: changed from adjacent to potential (E2); the only AI output is the book (Dec 2023–Apr 2024), and I found no standing AI programme in 2024–26. Transferable method: relevance realisation and the 'ecology of practices' for cultivating wisdom, as a frame for alignment-as-wisdom and for AI's effect on meaning. Transfer: convening (J5); the book addresses his general audience. Status: changed, because the foundation's site has folded into his personal site. MISFIT: an individual-led platform.

name: Flourishing Intelligence Program (FLIP), Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing, University of Oxford
summary: A research programme launched in December 2025 in the Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing at Linacre College, Oxford, directed by neuroscientist Ruben Laukkonen with centre director Morten Kringelbach. It works on three layers. The human: neuroscience and contemplative practice. The interface: embodied human–AI interfaces, including meditation to improve the brain's signal-to-noise ratio for brain–computer interfaces. The AI: brain-inspired, energy-efficient architectures and 'intrinsic' alignment built on contemplative principles. It is part of the International Centre for Flourishing, with Gustavo Deco's group at Pompeu Fabra University (Barcelona) and Peter Vuust's Center for Music in the Brain (Aarhus).
why_it_matters: It is the institutional home of the 'Contemplative AI' agenda, which tests contemplative principles (mindfulness, emptiness, non-duality, boundless care) as alignment interventions, and of 'Positive Alignment', which argues that alignment should aim at flourishing as well as harm prevention. Here contemplative knowledge is turned into alignment proposals that can be tested.

key_work.title: Contemplative Artificial Intelligence (published in AGI-25 proceedings as 'Contemplative Superalignment')
Positive Alignment: Artificial Intelligence for Human Flourishing
From cacophony to hierarchy: a principled framework for assessing AI consciousness

people: Shamil Chandaria (Senior Advisor and founding member)
funding: A donation from the Cillo family; amount not disclosed.
status_evidence: Sep 2026: FLIP's Laukkonen and Kringelbach co-authored 'From cacophony to hierarchy' on assessing AI consciousness; May 2026: 'Positive Alignment' paper; Jul 2026: 'Clear Mind' paper on meditation and neural signal-to-noise.
engage: 'Collaborate with us' contact and news sign-up on theflip.ai
Team of postdocs and PhD students; no open positions listed
caveats: FLIP launched in December 2025, so its track record is short. The Contemplative AI paper (first posted April 2025) predates FLIP and was carried into it. The reported gains come from prompting experiments, and the claims about intrinsic alignment have not been demonstrated. The discovery notes mention a partnership with Positive AI Labs and retreats with the Wisdom + AI Network; neither appears on FLIP's site, and I did not verify them. Many listed researchers are shared with the Barcelona and Aarhus partner groups.
tag_notes: Home: contemplative, cont_science (B1). The taxonomy names FLIP, and its alignment proposals are built from contemplative principles; life (neuroscience, active inference) and minds (the AI-consciousness framework, Sep 2026) are secondary. Ring: bridge, kept (E3). It is a programme inside an existing Oxford flourishing centre, rooted in neuroscience and contemplative science, that explicitly asks how to build 'safe superintelligence'; it was not founded inside the AI-safety ecosystem, so not core. Transfer: into_model (J1). It tests contemplative principles as prompting and constitutional interventions and works on brain-inspired architectures. Quadrants: It+I, as in G. Badge: full_spectrum, since it uses contemplative insight as method alongside experiments. org_type: programme (A1, a unit within a university centre).

name: Monash Centre for Consciousness and Contemplative Studies (M3CS)
summary: A Monash University centre in Melbourne, directed by the philosopher Jakob Hohwy, that combines consciousness science, active inference, philosophy of mind, contemplative studies and interfaith dialogue, and teaches contemplative practice to students and workplaces. It was established in 2021 with a A$12 million grant from the Three Springs Foundation. Its AI work is a minority strand. Hohwy and Lars Sandved-Smith are co-authors of 'Contemplative Artificial Intelligence' (2025, led by Ruben Laukkonen), which proposes mindfulness, emptiness, non-duality and boundless care as alignment principles that active-inference architectures could implement, and other members have published on AI and nondual understanding.
why_it_matters: It sets out a concrete route from contemplative traditions to alignment targets and agent design, using active inference, and has run first prompt-level tests on safety benchmarks and the Prisoner's Dilemma. Mainstream alignment rarely draws on this source of values.

key_work.title: Contemplative Artificial Intelligence (Laukkonen, Inglis, Chandaria, Sandved-Smith, Lopez-Sola, Hohwy, Gold, Elwood)
Contemplative superalignment (AGI-25 conference proceedings, Reykjavik)
Can AI facilitate genuine nondualist understanding? (Krägeloh and Berryman, Topoi, accepted)
Composing the Self: Writing and the Cultivation of the 'Human' in the Shadow of AI (project, Hohwy as chief investigator)

people: Lars Sandved-Smith (computational neuroscientist; co-author of Contemplative AI)
funding: A$12 million philanthropic grant (2021) from Martin and Loreto Hosking's Three Springs Foundation; some project funding from private donors and Australian government programmes (e.g. a 2025 regional religious-literacy programme).
status_evidence: Mar 2026: members published 'Active inference, computational phenomenology, and advanced meditation' (Neuroscience and Biobehavioral Reviews); 2026: 'Can AI facilitate genuine nondualist understanding?' accepted in Topoi; May 2026: partner in Mindful May at Monash.
engage: Contemplative-studies units, plus professional-development training for workplaces (not AI-specific)
Mindful May at Monash, an annual month of mindfulness events (May 2026)
Research collaboration on contemplative AI and active inference through Hohwy's group
caveats: The Contemplative AI paper was led by Ruben Laukkonen (Southern Cross University); M3CS is the affiliation of two of its eight authors, so attributing it to the centre overstates the centre's own AI programme. Most of the centre's work (consciousness science, interreligious history, religious literacy) is not about AI. Monash's site sits behind a bot check, so I took details from search snippets, Monash's research portal and the 2021 launch article rather than the live pages. The benchmark results come from prompting only and are preliminary.
tag_notes: Home contemplative (B1, B4; taxonomy worked example 1): its AI output, Contemplative AI, is a design proposal built from contemplative insight, with secondary traditions in consciousness science and active inference (life). Ring bridge, kept from the roster and worked example: the centre is rooted in consciousness and contemplative studies, and its AI line runs 2025-26 (Contemplative AI paper, AGI-25 paper, 2025 AI project, 2026 Topoi paper), though it is thin and carried by a few members. Transfer into_model (J1): the principles are meant to be built into model constitutions, architectures and reinforcement. Badge full_spectrum: it pairs first-person contemplative knowledge with active-inference modelling and benchmark tests as its method. Engagement coded from search snippets of its own pages, because the live site was blocked.

name: Re-Align: Workshop on Representational Alignment
summary: An annual workshop at ICLR (2024, 2025, 2026) where machine-learning, neuroscience and cognitive-science researchers work on measuring and using the similarity between the internal representations of brains, humans and neural networks. The third edition (27 April 2026) asked 'what can we do with alignment?', with two themes: neural control, which it links to mechanistic interpretability and to building safer, steerable models, and downstream behaviour. It added the Re-Align Challenge, a hackathon with blue-team and red-team tracks and a leaderboard of representational-comparison measures. Eight researchers from EPFL, MIT/UCSF, MPI Psycholinguistics, NYU, Berkeley, Stanford and UW-Madison organise it.
why_it_matters: It is a standing venue where the methods cognitive scientists and neuroscientists use to compare minds reach interpretability and steering research. Related submissions to ICLR grew from 303 (2024) to 688 (2026), so it is an entry point for funders looking for cognitive-science routes into understanding models.

key_work.title: Re-Align Workshop @ ICLR 2026: neural control and downstream behaviour
Re-Align Challenge (hackathon and leaderboard of representational-comparison measures)
Re-Align Workshop @ ICLR 2026 listing (ICLR virtual site)

funding: Not disclosed. The 2026 edition offered travel grants to accepted authors but did not name the funder.
status_evidence: 27 Apr 2026: third Re-Align workshop held at ICLR 2026, with the first Re-Align Challenge (submissions closed 26 Feb 2026).
engage: Submit papers to future editions (the 2026 call closed 5 Feb 2026, via OpenReview)
Enter the Re-Align Challenge, which is run online
Attend at ICLR; the 2026 edition offered asynchronous virtual presentation and travel grants
caveats: 'Alignment' here mainly means similarity between representations, not value alignment. The safety framing is a single line in the 2026 call, so 'bridge' depends on the interpretability and steerability theme. No 2027 edition had been announced at the time of writing. As a workshop series it has no staff or institution of its own, and the organisers change from year to year.
tag_notes: Home psych (B5): cognitive science and experiments comparing models with humans; neuroscience is secondary (life). Ring bridge, kept from the roster: a repeated convening (three editions, 2024-26) whose 2026 theme explicitly ties representational alignment to interpretability and 'safer, steerable models'; that framing is thin. Transfer into_model: the methods aim at reading and controlling model representations. Org type programme (I): a workshop series hosted at ICLR. Online hub: the challenge can be entered remotely. MISFIT: framing, since the series states no stakes; 'flourishing' is the nearest fit for its 'what can we do with alignment?' theme.

name: Bramley Computational Cognitive Science Lab (University of Edinburgh)
summary: Neil Bramley's group in Edinburgh's School of Philosophy, Psychology and Language Sciences studies how people learn causal structure, generalise, generate hypotheses and learn from others. It combines behavioural experiments with adults and children with computational models. Its link to AI safety is one event: with UK AISI's Konstantinos Voudouris and Christopher Summerfield, Harvard's Xavier Roberts-Gaal and NYU's Ilia Sucholutsky, Bramley co-organised the half-day workshop 'The Cognitive Science of AI Alignment' at CogSci 2026 (Rio de Janeiro, 22-25 July 2026). The workshop was built around four questions: what the alignment target is, how weaker agents can supervise stronger ones, how interacting with AI changes human values, and what human feedback actually measures.
why_it_matters: The lab's computational accounts of how people learn structure and norms from sparse data, and of the biases in their judgements, bear directly on what an alignment target is and how reliable human feedback is. The CogSci 2026 workshop, run with UK AISI, is an early attempt to recruit cognitive scientists into alignment work.

key_work.title: The Cognitive Science of AI Alignment (CogSci 2026 workshop; Voudouris, Roberts-Gaal, Bramley, Sucholutsky, Summerfield)
Resource bottlenecks determine when human and machine teams decide to specialise
Partner Modelling Emerges in Recurrent Agents (But Only When It Matters)

people: Neil R. Bramley (PI; Reader in Psychology)
funding: EPSRC New Investigator Award 'Computational Constructivism: The Algorithmic Basis of Discovery' (2021-2024). The workshop's closing session pointed attendees to UK AISI funding and collaboration routes.
status_evidence: Jul 2026: co-organised 'The Cognitive Science of AI Alignment' workshop at CogSci 2026 (published in the Proceedings of the Cognitive Science Society, vol. 48).
engage: Door to open: approach Neil Bramley about cognitive-science collaborations on value learning, generalisation or biases in human feedback
PhD study in computational cognitive science at Edinburgh
caveats: The roster calls 'The cognitive science of AI alignment' a paper, but it is a workshop proposal published in the CogSci proceedings. UK AISI staff led it (Voudouris is first author), and Bramley was one of five organisers and gave the talk 'Alignment as plumbing, partnering, or parenting'. The lab has no other AI-safety output, though some of its papers cover human-machine teaming and artificial agents. I lowered the ring from bridge to potential for this reason.
tag_notes: Home psych (H1, B5): computational cognitive science of causal and concept learning. Ring changed from bridge to potential (E2): its only AI-safety output is one co-organised workshop, and the bridge rules say a single workshop is potential. Transferable method: computational models of how humans learn causal structure, concepts and values from sparse data, and of systematic biases in judgement and social learning, applicable to alignment targets and to correcting human-feedback signals. Transfer into_model, not none_yet: the workshop aims at how AI systems are aligned and overseen. Framing taken from the workshop text ('alarmingly' exceeding humans; supervising stronger agents), which UK AISI co-wrote, so confidence is low. Engagement 'partner' because it has no AI programme.

name: NYU Center for Mind, Ethics, and Policy (CMEP)
summary: A New York University centre, directed by the philosopher Jeff Sebo, that researches the consciousness, sentience, agency and moral, legal and political status of nonhuman minds, with a special focus on animals and AI systems. It began in 2022 as the Mind, Ethics, and Policy Program and became a permanent centre in 2024 with a $6 million endowment. It publishes research, advises decision-makers, and runs field-building events: an annual summit, public talks, and workshops such as one on welfare comparisons between species and substrates (April 2026). Its AI outputs include 'Taking AI Welfare Seriously' (2024, with Eleos AI) and a 2025 paper arguing there is a moderately strong tension between AI-safety measures and AI welfare.
why_it_matters: It brings animal-sentience science and moral philosophy into AI welfare. It has argued in print that safety measures such as constraint, deception, surveillance, alteration and deletion raise welfare questions if AI systems matter morally, a tension that mainstream safety work largely ignores.

key_work.title: Taking AI Welfare Seriously (Long, Sebo, Butlin et al.; co-sponsored with Eleos AI)
Is There a Tension between AI Safety and AI Welfare? (Long, Sebo, Sims, Philosophical Studies)
What will society think about AI consciousness? Lessons from the animal case (Caviola, Sebo, Birch, Trends in Cognitive Sciences)
NYU 2026 Mind, Ethics, and Policy Summit and Workshop on Interspecies and Intersubstrate Welfare Comparisons

funding: $6 million endowment (announced July 2024): $5 million from The Navigation Fund and $1 million from Polaris Ventures. It also takes donations to a spend-down fund.
status_evidence: 2 Sep 2026: public event 'What Does Claude's J-Space Tell Us About Consciousness?' with Jack Lindsey and Patrick Butlin; 2 Jul 2026: 'Studying AI Welfare Empirically' (Campbell, Long, Sebo).
